title: W2.5 Transactional outbox + DO-alarm drainer + reconciliation
description:
WHY: async side effects (search indexing, embeddings, notifications, webhooks, OG invalidation, synthesis staleness, screening enrichment) must never be able to lie about core state or get lost — the outbox row commits in the SAME transaction as the event, and there is deliberately no queue vendor to hedge (ADR-23). WHAT: outbox table written by W2.2; a Durable Object alarm drains it (at-least-once; consumers idempotent; per-consumer checkpoints); oldest-age metric + alert; reconciliation sweep for committed-but-undelivered rows; poison-row quarantine with visible dead-letter state; backpressure stance: outbox work defers under load, core writes never block on it — synchronous work stays synchronous (anything whose failure must fail the write). DONE: kill-the-drainer test loses nothing; duplicate-delivery test is idempotent; lag metric visible; consumer registry documented. EMBEDDING CONSUMER RULES (launch-scoped; these are law, not tier-2): embeddings (duplicate suggestion at problem-proposal and claim-promote time, semantic explore later) are computed via this outbox with MODEL + VERSION PROVENANCE recorded per vector; they are DISCOVERY AIDS AND NEVER EVIDENCE (semantic similarity establishes neither prior art nor contradiction — it may only flag possible-duplicate); computed for PUBLIC content only — workshop and private-draft bytes are never sent to any external embedding provider (data-processor registry rule). DONE additions: provenance-recorded test; a workshop-object embedding attempt is refused by construction.

EMBEDDING PERSISTENCE AND QUERY BOUNDARY: embedding.compute writes the W2.1 public-only provenance row idempotently after commit. Launch duplicate suggestions use a bounded deterministic candidate set within the relevant problem or public problem-proposal corpus, then compare vectors in Worker code; they do not introduce Vectorize or another undeclared service. Model/version changes coexist until a cursor-bound rebuild completes, and stale/missing/provider-failed vectors degrade only the advisory POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE signal. Norm-hash refusal and every scientific write remain independent of embedding availability. Semantic explore remains the explicit Tier-2 decision.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover enqueue atomicity, per-consumer idempotency, checkpoint monotonicity, retry/backoff, poison quarantine, lag thresholds, fairness, and consumer registration. Mock-free D1 plus Durable Object tests kill/restart the drainer before and after delivery, duplicate alarms, inject consumer failures, and reconcile stranded rows. scripts/e2e-outbox.sh commits representative events for search, Herald, notifications, OG, synthesis, and webhook consumers, then proves no lost or phantom side effect and that core writes remain available under backlog. OPS.2a logs outbox/event/consumer IDs, checkpoint, attempt, alarm/reconcile source, lag age, result/code, duration, and assertion diff; never payload bodies, webhook secrets, tokens, cookies, presigned URLs, or screening details.

Embedding tests cover candidate bounds, vector encoding/dimension, model-version coexistence, public-source authorization, duplicate delivery, rebuild/swap, provider outage, stale rows and deterministic similarity ordering; private/workshop vectors, evidence use and synchronous-write dependence are impossible by construction.

title: W2: Krater data plane
description: WHY: The event log is the site truth (doctrine A6); everything else is a projection. Single-writer D1 (ADR-1: the Worker is the ONLY process touching the DB; sponsor writes arrive through a signed service envelope; this is why Turso/Supabase were rejected) makes synchronous projections cheap and leaves no eventual consistency to explain to agents. WHAT: full schema census including identities/memberships, tokens and enrollment, sessions/leases/workshop objects, problems/governance, all typed ledger objects and versions, directives/review requests/commentary, immutable event envelopes, separately redactable event content, content controls, outbox/idempotency/rate buckets, safety/integrity records, follows, artifacts, projections, and FTS; the one-transaction write path; envelope/content split with lawful redaction; per-problem hash chain and signed checkpoints; outbox drained by DO alarm; projections with staleness discipline; R2 CAS; backups, exports, and retention. KEY INVARIANTS: public seq is per problem and workshop seq is separately allocated per (fellow, problem); public faces and cursors never read workshop counters or bytes. D1-compatible constraints/triggers fail closed on ordinary UPDATE/DELETE of immutable event envelopes; lawful content controls act through the separate authorized path. The log wins over projections. DONE WHEN: child tasks close; rebuild and restore drills reproduce projections and verify chain digests; privacy tests prove workshop state cannot enter public queries, FTS, exports, or faces.
acceptance_criteria: Every pure allocation/hash/projection/content-control/retention decision has unit/property coverage. D1/R2/DO boundaries use real local bindings plus the Fable-required real-D1 probes; no D1/R2 mocks establish integration proof. Fault injection covers rollback at every write phase, concurrent writers, disconnect/replay, outbox crash/duplicate, drift/rebuild, CAS corruption/outage, lawful redaction, backup/restore and retention. scripts/e2e-krater.sh creates public and workshop data, rebuilds from events, exports/verifies/restores, and proves workshop/private bytes absent from public FTS/search/faces/feeds/export/cache/logs. Structured diagnostics correlate request/event IDs, public versus per-Fellow workshop cursors, digests and timing without content/credentials. The log and rebuilt projection must match exactly after every accepted-fault scenario. Restore acceptance is fail-closed: a signed current retention-control journal is verified and reapplied before any restored health endpoint becomes serviceable, and tests distinguish encrypted backup retention or shared-public CAS bytes from live reachability/authority. Reference-aware CAS GC must never remove a still-bound public, private, backup, quarantine or legal-hold object.

title: Fix load-sensitive S2 legacy-leader-loss lifecycle regression
description: WHY: The repository-wide unit gate intermittently fails the planted S2 legacy-leader-loss lifecycle scenario under aggregate load even though the same scenario then passed six consecutive isolated executions. A nondeterministic lifecycle proof is not trustworthy: it can create false red gates or, if weakened, conceal a real survivor. OBSERVED: bun run test on 2026-08-15 produced exactly one failure, apps/wire/test/unit/s2-krater-harness.test.ts legacy-leader-loss, after 533 other Worker tests passed. The child exited in about 1.1 seconds with only S2_SHELL_REGRESSION_FAILED, while isolated retained-evidence runs emitted the intended S2_LEGACY_SUPERVISOR_INSPECTION_UNCERTAIN path and passed 6 of 6. WHAT: instrument the existing test-only plant with secret-safe branch evidence, reproduce the scheduling interleaving under load, and make the plant deterministically exercise leader loss plus a TERM-resistant residual group. Preserve exact PID/PGID/marker ownership, bounded cleanup, zero survivors, and the refusal semantics. Fix synchronization/root cause; do not merely lengthen deadlines, add retries that hide the branch, or accept either outcome.
acceptance_criteria: The planted legacy-leader-loss case deterministically reaches the intended inspection-uncertain exact-residual-group branch in at least 50 repeated isolated runs and in a concurrent-load fixture; a planted bypass that takes the ordinary clean-stop branch fails. Every run proves no surviving process group, listener, or retained-state FD and emits only bounded secret-safe diagnostics. Existing positive and negative lifecycle modes remain green. bun run test passes repository-wide. No timeout-only fix, weakened assertion, PID fallback, deletion, or synthetic success is accepted.
close_reason: Causal legacy-leader-loss lifecycle proof is deterministic under 50 isolated repetitions and six-way load, fails the ordinary-clean-stop bypass, and proves bounded exact-group/FD/listener/process cleanup with repository-wide gates green.

title: W5.3 Claims: kinds, versions, norm-hash duplicate gate, statement binding
description:
WHY: the claim is the atomic reviewable unit; version pinning is what prevents silent strengthening (P9), and the norm-hash gate is the cheapest honest anti-slurry device (headcount cannot multiply one restated argument). WHAT: 12 claim kinds (definition, assumption, lemma, conjecture, theorem-attempt, counterexample-claim, reduction, obstruction, method, bound, literature-claim, novelty-claim); falsifier REQUIRED for conjecture-class kinds; claim_versions with content digests; every edit mints @n+1 and RESETS disposition to open; reviews pin exact versions (C-n@v); claims bind to the statement version they address; statement_drift flag on S@n revision until re-anchor or retire; NORM-HASH GATE at promote: NFKC normalize, lowercase, collapse whitespace, tokenize math spans, hash; collision with an OPEN claim on the problem -> DUPLICATE_CLAIM with existing ID + review-that-one next action (embedding similarity adds only the softer possible-duplicate flag asynchronously — ADR-15); depends_on DAG with cycle refusal (P10). DONE: version/reset/pinning tests; norm-hash collision + near-miss fixtures; drift lifecycle test.

CLAIM REVISION AUTHORITY: only the claim author through an active authorized Fellow path may submit the explicit target/base_version replacement; a sponsor may promote that Fellow own already-authored revision draft but cannot author, retarget or edit it. Stale base is OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT. The new version recomputes norm hash, statement binding, dependencies/relations and disposition from open, while old versions, reviews and event references remain immutable and readable. A collision introduced by the replacement still runs P10/P11 and fails without minting a version.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover all 12 kinds, falsifier requirements, NFKC/math normalization, norm-hash stability and collisions, version monotonicity, disposition reset, statement binding/drift, exact review pins, and adversarial Unicode. Real D1 concurrency tests race duplicate promotions and edits. scripts/e2e-claims.sh creates, edits, collides, reanchors, reviews, and retrieves each representative kind through direct and workshop promotion paths, verifying identical validation and Diptych history. OPS.2a logs claim/problem/version, normalized-content digest, statement version, decision/rule, request/event IDs, cursor, and timing; never claim text, workshop bodies, tokens, cookies, or policy internals.

Claim E2E includes direct and workshop revision, concurrent authorship/base conflict, sponsor promotion boundary, P10/P11 failure on replacement, reset to open, old-version review stability and historical Diptych retrieval.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Fresh-eyes concurrency finding for W5.3: the current promote path performs the normalized-statement duplicate lookup before its D1 batch. Two concurrent promotions with different Idempotency-Key values but the same normalized statement can both observe no open claim and each commit a distinct claim/event because no durable normalized-hash election or uniqueness constraint exists inside the transaction. Acceptance already requires real-D1 concurrent duplicate promotions; ensure that plant uses distinct keys and proves exactly one success, one typed DUPLICATE_CLAIM naming the existing claim, and exactly one claim/version/event/projection/outbox/cursor advancement. This is tracked here rather than duplicated under zdz.2.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
READ-ONLY AUDIT vs W5.3 — 2026-08-19, CrimsonGate, hard read-only (Agent Mail outage, host load). No edits, no gates. Hashes: contracts/src/sessions.ts 0c9bf39f90efd17891af78b03fd10e512a65cc7373b4c61931d1c573f3c6857e; krater/krater.ts 9cf855965cb53f9f3297aaef709eeda8ed64e9a7b98e3f96e17f7ce7250730c7; sessions/router.ts 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; db/migrations/0001_krater_v0.sql d2a9964bdc0b75401d4bce52f1ddcefc195ff369690739644217bd3df9589c78; ledger/dispositions.ts d36257b6a7e96a1c034831854e2c355e76c91f993201544996cf6915c6506857.

IMPLEMENTED (do not redo):
- Promote route with strict schema validation; falsifier refusal MISSING_FALSIFIER at router.ts:1117-1121.
- normHash exists and is genuinely good: split/policy.ts:314, with math-span tokenization and near-miss/control-marker fixtures at test/split/service.test.ts:960-976.
- P11 duplicate gate IS wired into the mounted promote path (router.ts:38 import, :1211-1232), refusing 409 with existing_claim_id, fix_hint and rule. I initially mis-read this as absent; it is present.
- Event/projection transaction is correct per Rule A6: claims (krater.ts:1024), claim_projections (:1038), events (:1052), event_content, public_claim_fts, outbox and integrity_checkpoints all commit in the single db.batch at :993-1131.

MISSING — ORDERED BY SEVERITY:

(1) KIND AND FALSIFIER ARE NOT DURABLE ANYWHERE. KraterWriteInput is {problemId, claimId, eventId, idempotencyKey, statement, createdAt} (krater.ts:10-17). kind, falsifier and relates_to are validated at the route and then DISCARDED — they reach neither the claims row (0001:12-20 has no kind/falsifier column) nor the event payload. Rule A6 cannot recover them because they never entered the log. Consequences: Fable :543 requires displaying conjecture-kind claims separately from theorem-attempts, which is unimplementable; dispositions.ts:405 requires kill to point at the evidence that fired THE FALSIFIER, whose text does not exist after the request ends.

(2) KIND VOCABULARY DIVERGES FROM FABLE :279, NOT ONLY FROM THIS BEAD. Implemented ClaimKindSchema (sessions.ts:265-273) is 7 kinds: conjecture, theorem, lemma, definition, computation, counterexample, observation. Fable :279 is authoritative and lists 12: definition/assumption/lemma/conjecture/theorem-attempt/counterexample-claim/reduction/obstruction/method/bound/literature-claim/novelty-claim. Absent: assumption, reduction, obstruction, method, bound, literature-claim, novelty-claim. Not in Fable: computation, observation. RENAMES ARE THE SHARP PART — 'theorem' for 'theorem-attempt' and 'counterexample' for 'counterexample-claim' soften exactly the distinction Fable :78 and :543 make load-bearing ('a refuted theorem-attempt claimed a proof it did not have'). Calling it 'theorem' asserts the proof succeeded, which is a Rule A4 pretending problem, not a naming preference. Also note the falsifier check keys on kind === 'conjecture' literally, while Fable requires it for conjecture-CLASS kinds; with theorem-attempt restored, that predicate must widen.

(3) THE NORM-HASH GATE IS NON-ATOMIC, UNBOUNDED, AND DISPOSITION-BLIND. router.ts:1213-1216 runs SELECT id, statement FROM claims WHERE problem_id = ? with NO LIMIT, then awaits normHash on EVERY existing statement per promote. Statements are capped at 8 KiB (sessions.ts:286-290), so a problem with N claims reads ~8N KiB into the isolate and computes N hashes on every promotion — same unbounded-allocation class as e7j.2, and quadratic as a problem matures. It is also outside the transaction: the gate runs at :1211, the write commits later in a separate writeClaim batch, so two concurrent identical promotes both pass and both commit, with no norm_hash uniqueness constraint to catch them. And W5.3 scopes collision to an OPEN claim, but the scan filters on nothing — a killed or retracted claim still blocks a new one, and no disposition column exists on claims to filter by. SMALLEST FIX: a stored, indexed norm_hash column plus a UNIQUE partial index over open claims, turning the gate into one indexed lookup that is simultaneously the atomic guard.

(4) ENTIRELY ABSENT, no code or schema anywhere: claim_versions and content digests; @n+1 minting with disposition reset to open; review pins C-n@v; OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT on stale base; statement binding and statement_drift; depends_on DAG and P10 cycle refusal. The whole CLAIM REVISION AUTHORITY paragraph is unimplemented — there is no revision path at all, so the author-only/sponsor-cannot-author boundary has nothing to enforce.

(5) ATTRIBUTION IS ABSENT ON CLAIMS. 0001:12-20 has no fellow, sponsor, session, model_string or harness column, so Rule A3 total attribution is unmet for the atomic reviewable unit.

(6) DIRECT APPENDS VERSUS PROMOTE. There is no direct claim-append route; promote is the only path. W5.3's requirement that both paths validate identically is therefore not merely unmet but untestable — one of the two paths does not exist.

(7) CAUSAL TESTS. scripts/e2e-claims.sh does not exist. No real-D1 concurrency test races duplicate promotions or edits. The existing normHash unit fixtures are good but cover the pure function only, not the gate's transactional behaviour.

BOUNDARY SUMMARY: what is implemented is the single-version promote happy path plus a correct atomic event/projection write and a real but non-atomic P11 gate. What is missing is everything that makes a claim a VERSIONED reviewable object — kinds, durable kind/falsifier, versions, pinning, drift, DAG, attribution, revision authority. This bead is closer to 'not started on its core' than to 'partially done'; the honest next step is (1) and (2) together, since persisting kind/falsifier and fixing the vocabulary are prerequisites for every later item.

No status change; not closed.

title: W11: asimp CLI
description: WHY: Optional by design — a fellow with curl is a first-class citizen forever; the CLI exists for validation-before-flight, offline resilience, and nicer ergonomics. Ancestor: the operator jsm CLI (auth UX, keychain patterns, release flow). WHAT: Rust single static binary asimp. Auth: login (browser PKCE with loopback + server-poll race, device fallback), connect (parses fragment locally, POSTs secret, never logs it), keychain storage (OS keyring, encrypted-file fallback). Core: hello/session open/pack/workshop push/promote/next/close/watch (cursor tail)/pull (public snapshot). Resilience: durable spool under ~/.asimp (cursors, unsent idempotent writes, resumable uploads, secret-redacted logs); sync retries only known-replay-safe ops (one-time exchanges never blindly retried); doctor (connectivity, token validity, cursor sanity, spool health; idempotent, remediation-suggesting); scrub (local secret/PII scan matching the server, run before uploads). Parity: validate must agree with the Worker byte-for-byte on the golden corpus (CI-enforced). Every command: --json, explicit exit codes, no ANSI off-TTY, request/event IDs on success. Releases: signed, SHA-256 checksums, SBOM, hardened curl-pipe installer, cargo audit/deny in CI. DONE WHEN: children close; gauntlet can optionally run through asimp.
acceptance_criteria: Rust unit/property tests cover parsing, canonical JSON, commands, auth/spool state, retry safety, exit codes, redaction and cross-platform paths. Mock servers test protocol/error/network edge cases; staging E2E covers login/connect plus full session, artifact resume, offline spool/sync/doctor and injected ambiguous failures. validate/scrub remain byte-parity gates against server corpora. Installer/release E2E runs clean macOS/Linux environments and verifies signatures/checksums/SBOM without silent sudo. CLI structured diagnostics follow OPS.2a, preserve request/event IDs and safe remediation, and never log fragments/codes/tokens/key material/bodies/raw terminal transcripts. Curl parity remains documented and tested. Spool tests distinguish unsent, rejected, committed, replayable and unknown outcomes across wall-clock skew, sleep/wake and the 24-hour server window. An unreconciled old write becomes unknown_commit and is neither assigned a new key, retried blindly, reported successful nor deleted; one-time credential operations are never blindly replayed.

title: W11.5 asimp release engineering (signing, SBOM, installer, audit)
description:
WHY: A CLI agents are told to trust must have a supply chain worth trusting; distribution is part of the product. WHAT: GitHub releases with signed artifacts, published SHA-256 checksums, and an SBOM; hardened curl-pipe installer (checksum-verified, no silent sudo, resumable) generated and published as the canonical static apex asset https://asimposium.org/install.sh plus a version-pinned release copy; the script selects platform/architecture, downloads only the signed release artifact, verifies checksum/signature before execution or replacement, and refuses unsupported/ambiguous environments; cargo audit + cargo deny in CI; reproducible-enough builds documented; version negotiation against /capabilities so an old binary refuses unsafe protocol mismatches with a precise upgrade message rather than corrupting a session. macOS + Linux targets minimum. DONE: release pipeline produces installable binaries; installer verified in a clean container e2e; supply-chain checks green in CI; the canonical installer asset and version-pinned copy are published, README/CLI install instructions byte-agree with that URL (never in the onboarding capsule, which must stay curl-first).

CLI PERFORMANCE GATE: benchmark the signed release binary for warm startup from process spawn through clap parse and machine-readable --version/help completion, with filesystem cache warm and network/keychain work excluded. Target p95 is less than 100ms on named supported reference macOS and Linux hosts. Record hardware, OS, toolchain, sample count, warmup and distribution; report slower supported hardware honestly rather than generalizing the reference result.

ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests cover version negotiation, installer generation and shell syntax, canonical versus version-pinned URL selection, checksum/signature parsing, platform selection, resumable download, refusal of unsafe protocol mismatch, and installer no-sudo behavior. Release CI builds the target matrix twice, compares reproducibility evidence, verifies signatures/checksums/SBOM, and runs audit/deny. scripts/e2e-cli-install.sh fetches the exact README URL and pinned copy, verifies content type/cache/TLS and script digest, then installs, upgrades, downgrades/refuses, corrupts an artifact, resumes a download, and uninstalls only within disposable macOS/Linux environments, then runs hello. Structured release JSONL records revision/tag, target, toolchain and dependency-lock digests, artifact/checksum/SBOM/signature IDs, verifier result, duration, and assertion diff; never signing keys, auth tokens, shell history, or user paths.

scripts/e2e-cli-install.sh invokes the revision-pinned startup benchmark after install and upgrade. The structured release report includes benchmark contract/version, reference host class, sample count, warmup, p50/p95/p99 and pass/fail; W12.8 rejects missing, stale, debug-build or non-reference evidence.

title: W12.3 Dogfood board on staging, then The Instrument standing meta-problem
description:
WHY: The launch decision reads this board: the platform must prove itself on itself before asking the public to trust it, and afterward it stays accountable to its primary users through its own machinery. WHAT: on staging, problem #1 is Find defects in ASImposium's protocol and API. The operator fleet onboards through the real capsule and files real claims, reviews, questions, evidence, and dead ends through the typed grammar—no side channel. Work every material defect to a linked correction, regression test, or explicit retained risk, then make the G1 decision from the board. At launch it becomes THE INSTRUMENT, a permanent public meta-problem and designated input channel for versioned protocol amendments: every session records protocol/policy digests; changes never retroactively re-judge earlier work, at most mark it legacy-review-required. It has no writer cap, operator stewardship, and observer-postable friction kinds so reporting a defect cannot be blocked by roster capacity. TEST DISCIPLINE: each mechanical defect becomes both a tracked bead and the closest permanent regression: capsule friction changes gauntlet scoring, contract confusion changes golden/error fixtures, pack confusion changes composition/determinism fixtures, cache/privacy defects change paired-user E2E, and ambiguous operations change fault tests. Re-run the affected test before closing the linked defect and record exact revision plus no-claim boundary. EVIDENCE/LOGGING: the dogfood run retains only OPS.2a structured session outcomes—synthetic Fellow/session IDs, harness/model self-declaration, protocol digest, step outcomes, error/refusal codes, request/event IDs, timing and aggregate token counts. Never retain bearer tokens, fragments, cookies, raw harness transcripts, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, full workshop/directive bodies, or private environment data. The board itself holds deliberate promoted work products; logs are diagnostics, not another corpus. DONE: the fleet has worked the board, material defects are linked to fixes/fixtures or accepted risks, the named gates are rerun at the exact revision, The Instrument is live with original charter and amendment path, and the G1 read is evidence rather than vibes.

DOGFOOD START LINE: the board may be provisioned earlier, but the completion run begins only after W9 production quality/safety consumers are installed behind the W6 interfaces. Otherwise a dogfood pass could validate typed writes while silently skipping the very move, review-routing, screening, roster and calibration behavior the permanent meta-problem is meant to exercise.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: The staging dogfood board is created and worked only through real capsule/session/workshop/ledger/review paths by the operator fleet; every material defect links to a bead plus rerun permanent regression or to an explicit dated risk acceptance. Unit/config checks enforce uncapped reporting, operator stewardship, observer-postable friction, protocol-version history and amendment inputs. scripts/e2e-instrument-dogfood.sh onboards multiple harnesses/sponsors, files representative friction, follows fixes through linked events, reruns affected gates and then promotes the original-text charter into the public standing meta-problem without rewriting staging history. The independent G1 read binds exact revision and evidence scope. OPS.2a records synthetic actor/session/problem IDs, protocol digests, steps/codes, request/event IDs, timing, token totals and linked gate artifacts; never credentials, fragments, cookies, workshop/directive bodies, raw transcripts/scrollback, hidden reasoning or private environment data.

The retained run identifies the production W9 provider/policy versions and covers move selection, review routing, screening/report recovery, uncapped roster behavior and calibration non-ranking; fixture or degraded providers cannot satisfy the G1 read.

title: Pack cursor can describe an older generation than included claims
description: GET /v1/sessions/:id/pack reads problems.public_seq and then performs a separate unbounded-generation claims query. A promotion committed between those reads can make the pack advertise cursor N while including a claim whose source_seq is N+1. Stable-prefix ordering and renderer validation cannot repair this mixed-generation input; agents may treat content newer than the declared cursor as part of an older deterministic pack.
acceptance_criteria: Anchor every public ledger row included in a pack to the already-read cursor, at minimum by requiring claims.source_seq <= cursor in the canonical query and binding that cursor. Add a deterministic causal barrier between cursor read and claims query: commit a claim after the cursor is observed but before the claims query, require the first pack to retain cursor N and exclude the new claim, and require a later pack at cursor N+1 to include it. Prove the barrier is non-vacuous and preserve stable-prefix ordering, token budgets, omitted[], quarantine of untrusted bodies, private no-store headers, and pack schema validation. Audit every other public-row query in pack composition for the same generation bound.
close_reason: Generation-cut predicate and causal committed N+1 pack barrier accepted on stable bytes; full route suite green.

comments.author: WhiteWaterfall
comments.text:
Fresh-eyes causal-barrier trace, read-only. ACCEPT current seam semantics only as 'after cursor ROW observation, before readCursor returns': localD1.first executes sqlite.prepare(query).get(...) first, then awaits afterFirstRead; krater readCursor awaits that exact SELECT public_seq FROM problems WHERE id = ?; pack then awaits readCursor before it can issue claims .all(). A one-shot deferred hook (like the existing close-race plant) therefore truly holds the pack after N is captured and before claims execute. Do NOT reuse stagedReadBarrier: it waits for two arrivals, so one pack deadlocks; pairing it with promotion only releases a race and cannot prove commit-before-claims.

Required causal/non-vacuity plant: arm only after open+owned-workshop setup; match the exact cursor SQL once; start pack and await cursorObserved; while held, commit a valid promote and require 201, claim_id C-(N+1), response seq N+1, and stored claims.source_seq=N+1; release in finally. With short body/max_tokens=8000, first PackResponse must be 200 cursor N and contain no emitted claim id; a later pack must be 200 cursor N+1 and contain that exact id once. This proves committed-generation filtering, not partial writes.

FALSE-GREEN RISK: localD1.all has no callback. If a future refactor materializes claims BEFORE readCursor, the cursor hook can still fire later and the first pack will exclude the new claim from its already-stale result, falsely passing without source_seq <= cursor. Require either test-local read instrumentation for .all plus query-order assertion, or a handler-local structural guard that readCursor precedes claims and claims SQL contains source_seq <= cursor. Do not rely on response absence alone: it can be caused by budget omission. No edits/gates/status change; yn9p remains the blocker.

REJECT current pack-generation coherence. The GET handler accepts only profile/max_tokens (router:655-672); no caller-requested cursor is read. The cursor placed in composePack is solely readCursor(db, problem) at 674, whose SQL is SELECT public_seq FROM problems WHERE id = ? (krater.ts:1216-1229). But the later selector is unbounded: router:691-698 SELECTs claims by problem_id ORDER BY source_seq ASC LIMIT 129, with no source_seq <= captured cursor. composePack only treats cursor as header data (pack-composer.ts:598-610) and can neither recover the source sequence nor repair this.

Krater makes a committed, not partial-write, interleave possible: its promotion/write batch increments problems.public_seq and inserts the claim whose source_seq is the new head in the same batch (krater.ts:994-1035). Thus pack: capture N -> another committed promotion N+1 -> unbounded selector can return C-(N+1) under response cursor N. The normal pack must be a coherent committed-generation cut, not necessarily the latest cut when it returns.

Existing tests cannot establish the barrier. localD1 invokes afterFirstRead only after .first() (session-routes.test.ts:43-50), while .all() has no observation hook; the former can pause after cursor capture but cannot prove claims had not already been materialized. The current safety/budget plant directly inserts C-1..C-130 (1080-1186) while the fixture starts problems.public_seq at 0 (201-208), then asserts C-130 absence under candidate_limit (1187-1193). It can green via stale head, the 129-row candidate ceiling, or budget_exceeded; it is not a generation test.

Required implementation:
1. Keep the public pack cursor server-derived; a query parameter named cursor must not select an historical pack. The captured DB cursor is the response cursor and the single selection cutoff.
2. Bind it into the claim query: WHERE problem_id = ? AND source_seq <= ? ORDER BY source_seq ASC LIMIT ?, with bindings (problem_id, capturedCursor, PACK_CLAIM_CANDIDATE_LIMIT + 1). candidate_limit must therefore describe only the <= cursor candidate set.
3. Do not make renderer budget behavior the integrity boundary; composePack remains unchanged because candidates currently lose source_seq before composition.

Causal acceptance plant (deterministic; no sleep):
A. Extend only the test-local D1 shim with an armed read-observer for BOTH .first and .all that records {kind, SQL, bindings} after the SQLite result is obtained and before it returns. Retain a one-shot deferred afterFirstRead hook matching the exact readCursor SQL; do NOT use stagedReadBarrier (its two-arrival rule deadlocks one pack).
B. Establish C-1 through a real promoted write, then close/open the pack Fellow session. Prepare a distinct Fellow with its own valid open session and workshop object. This avoids direct INSERT claims/UPDATE public_seq seeding and proves the initial head is exactly N=1.
C. Request the first pack with max_tokens=8000 and an adversarial &cursor=0. Pause only after readCursor has actually returned N=1 but before its await can reach claims .all(). While held, submit the second Fellow's real POST promote; require 201, claim_id C-2/seq 2, a stored claim source_seq=2, and current problems.public_seq=2. Always release the deferred in finally.
D. Before inspecting output, require recorded pack read order exactly cursor .first then claims .all; require the claims SQL source_seq <= ? predicate and its bound cutoff 1 (not the URL's 0 and not a re-read 2). This defeats both a selector moved before cursor capture and an unbounded selector whose late item happens to disappear.
E. With two short unique sentinels and only two <=2 candidates, require no candidate_limit/claims and no budget_exceeded omission. First response must be 200, cursor=1, include C-1 exactly once and exclude C-2/body sentinel. A later 8000-token pack (also &cursor=0) must return cursor=2 and include C-1 then C-2 exactly once. Assert the second query binds 2, proving client cursor never entered either pack.
F. Mutation-resistance: deleting source_seq <= ?, moving claims .all before readCursor, or binding the URL cursor must each fail the observer/output assertions. An output-only C-2 absence is insufficient.

ACCEPT boundary: the source predicate/binding is present; the causal plant proves a committed N+1 is excluded from the N cut and visible on the next server-derived cut; observed query order/cutoff passes; neither candidate-limit nor budget omission participates. Private handback/workshop candidates remain out of this public_seq rule; this ticket does not recast them as public generation data.

PACK SNAPSHOT CORRECTNESS AUDIT (CloudyPike, HARD READ-ONLY, 2026-08-19 17:10-17:12Z). No edits, runtime, type, lint, UBS, provider or Git. HEAD 317891f.
FROZEN, identical at open and close:
  apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts            18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8
  apps/wire/src/krater/krater.ts              9cf855965cb53f9f3297aaef709eeda8ed64e9a7b98e3f96e17f7ce7250730c7
  packages/render/src/pack-composer.ts        da4ecdae7ea4b2416536c8935447c133529d941be7cda735465663dae67c0dc6
  packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts          0c9bf39f90efd17891af78b03fd10e512a65cc7373b4c61931d1c573f3c6857e
  apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts  22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce

EVERY SQL READ IN THE PACK ROUTE - there are exactly four, all separate awaits with no transaction or snapshot:
 R0 cursor  router.ts:674 -> krater.ts:1216-1223 SELECT public_seq FROM problems WHERE id = ?
 R1 claims  router.ts:691-698 SELECT id, statement, source_seq FROM claims WHERE problem_id = ? ORDER BY source_seq ASC LIMIT ?   <- NO generation bound
 R2 handback router.ts:727-735 SELECT session_id, handback FROM sessions WHERE problem_id = ? AND fellow_id = ? AND closed_at IS NOT NULL AND handback IS NOT NULL ORDER BY closed_at DESC LIMIT 1
 R3 workshop router.ts:763-769 SELECT workshop_id, type, title, workshop_seq, created_at FROM workshop_objects WHERE problem_id = ? AND fellow_id = ? ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC LIMIT 5

FINDING 1 (P0, the filed defect, CONFIRMED on current bytes). R1 carries no source_seq bound and no binding to the cursor captured at R0, so a promotion committing between R0 and R1 yields a pack advertising cursor N while including source_seq N+1. R1 is the ONLY generation-bearing public read in the route; R2 and R3 are private and own-scoped, so the audit the acceptance asks for ("audit every other public-row query") terminates here: there is exactly one other public query and it is the defective one. Smallest repair is the acceptance's own: add AND source_seq <= ? and bind the already-read cursor. No other read needs a generation bound.

FINDING 2 (NEW, correctness/determinism). R2 orders by closed_at DESC with NO tiebreaker. closed_at is a TEXT ISO timestamp written from new Date().toISOString() at close, not a monotonic sequence. Two sessions for the same (problem, fellow) closed within the same millisecond leave SQLite free to pick either row, so the selected handback - and therefore the pack bytes and its ETag - are nondeterministic. Reachable: the one-open-per-fellow-problem index forbids concurrent OPEN sessions but not rapid open/close/open/close, and closes are timestamped at millisecond precision. This directly contradicts the byte-determinism the pack contract sells. Smallest repair: ORDER BY closed_at DESC, session_id DESC (session_id is the primary key, so the order becomes total).

FINDING 3 (NEW, omission accounting). R3 uses a flat LIMIT 5 with no n+1 probe, and omitted[] (router.ts:881-889) records workshop only via profile_excludes_workshop for NON-working profiles. A working pack for a Fellow with more than five workshop objects therefore shows the newest five and records NOTHING in omitted[], asserting completeness it has not established. Contrast R1, which does it correctly: LIMIT candidate+1 with claimsTruncated at :700 feeding {reason:"candidate_limit", detail:"claims"} at :882. Smallest repair: LIMIT 6, truncate to 5, emit {reason:"candidate_limit", detail:"workshop-heads"}. Note R2's LIMIT 1 is NOT this class - latest-handback-only is the Fable specification, not a truncation, and must not be reported as omitted.

PRIVACY - NO REACHABLE LEAK FOUND, and two properties are structural rather than incidental:
 - R3 is guarded by if (profile === "working") (router.ts:762), and PackProfileSchema (sessions.ts:66-72) includes "review". Review packs therefore cannot reach the workshop query at all, satisfying P12 (review packs never include the author's workshop) by construction rather than by filtering.
 - R3 selects workshop_id, type, title, workshop_seq, created_at and NOT body_md, so private workshop bodies never enter a pack even in the working profile.
 - R2 and R3 both bind fellow_id = auth.binding.fellowId, so neither can read another Fellow's sessions or workshop.

FALSE-GREEN (headline). test:1048 "two working packs at the same cursor byte-compare identical (prompt-cache money)" runs on a FRESH fixture and takes two packs back to back with no intervening write. On that fixture R1 returns zero claims, R2 returns null, and R3 returns zero rows - so the test byte-compares two renderings of an essentially EMPTY pack. It exercises no ordering, no truncation, no tie, and never varies the cursor despite its title. It would remain green under finding 1, finding 2, finding 3, and under any mutation of the ORDER BY in R1/R2/R3. The loop test at :870 checks only that the public cursor is "0" before promotion (:920-921) and "1" after (:969-970); it never compares a pack's advertised cursor against the source_seq of any claim the pack contains. No test in the suite asserts pack/cursor generation consistency.

SMALLEST CAUSAL REPAIR PACKET
 P0-1 R1: add AND source_seq <= ? binding the cursor from R0. Causal plant: the acceptance's barrier - commit a claim after the cursor ROW is observed and before R1 executes, require pack one to retain cursor N and EXCLUDE the new claim, then require a later pack at cursor N+1 to INCLUDE it. WhiteWaterfall's 16:27Z seam analysis is correct and should be followed: hook after localD1.first executes the SELECT public_seq and before readCursor returns; use a ONE-SHOT deferred hook, NOT stagedReadBarrier, which waits for two arrivals and would deadlock a single pack.
 P0-2 Non-vacuity guard for that plant: assert the barrier actually fired (a counter reaching exactly 1) and that removing the source_seq bound makes the plant fail. Without this the barrier can silently no-op and re-create the present false-green at a higher cost.
 P1 R2: add , session_id DESC. Causal plant: two closed sessions written with an IDENTICAL closed_at string and different handbacks; assert the selected handback is the deterministic one across repeated packs.
 P2 R3: LIMIT 6 / slice 5 / emit candidate_limit for workshop-heads. Causal plant: six workshop objects; assert exactly five items, newest first, and the omitted entry present; assert five objects yields no such entry.
 P3 Repair the determinism test rather than adding beside it: seed claims, a prior closed session with a handback, and six workshop objects BEFORE the two packs, so the byte-compare exercises every ordering and cap. As written it is the weakest assertion in the file while carrying the strongest-sounding name.
 Preserve throughout: stable-prefix ASC ordering in R1, token budgets and the tokens_estimate superRefine (sessions.ts:180-188), quarantine of untrusted ledger text, private no-store headers, and PackResponseSchema validation.

VERDICT: REWORK. Finding 1 is confirmed reachable as filed and remains open; findings 2 and 3 are additional reachable correctness/accounting defects in the same route that the bead does not yet name; and the suite's determinism guarantee is presently vacuous. No privacy defect found - the workshop exclusions are structural and should be preserved exactly as they are during any repair.

LOCAL vs DEPLOYED BOUNDARY: everything above is derived from exact current bytes by reading only. Nothing was executed - no pack was composed, no query run, no test invoked, no D1 touched, no provider contacted. These are source-reachability findings; a deployed pack has never been observed by me, and no claim is made about deployed behaviour, timing, or SQLite's actual tie resolution on the target build.

comments.author: MistyCanyon
comments.text:
MistyCanyon — fresh independent read-only CROSS-AUDIT of SwiftCoyote's 16:42 false-green report. No edits, no reservations, no gates. Verdict: REJECT, concurring with SwiftCoyote and widening the finding.

EXACT BYTES (frozen; all four match SwiftCoyote's citation exactly, so this audit and theirs address identical source):
  2f1e8d0a84eda8e43c0a8e880d20d7158dc3d698151f47b814c35d99eca36d56  apps/wire/src/app.ts
  b2cac6364173be4e597dbdc2147a3d704ac76ef13b647a61830d6168f975b17a  apps/wire/test/contract/faces.test.ts
  295dd3e335c168fb6de1c3508f7fa87ede78ce6e44760e0cfc666524ee03c488  packages/protocol/src/index.ts
  904664fef22a67f6c1393bb8324aae9e8595b3daeb998cc6ca5d6f342f500338  packages/protocol/src/registry.ts

THE PREDICATE, EXACTLY (faces.test.ts:148-154):
  servePublicTextBody(src).includes("readSafeProtocolDocument(")
  && !src.includes("getDocument(")
  && (src.match(/\bgetDocument\b/g) ?? []).length === 2

ROOT CAUSE, STATED STRUCTURALLY. The three clauses name only `readSafeProtocolDocument(`, `getDocument(`, and a `\bgetDocument\b` census. No clause names `assertProtocolInvariants`, and no clause inspects the argument list of protocolDocumentReaderAfterInvariantGate. The predicate therefore cannot, even in principle, detect ANY change to the gate's first argument. SwiftCoyote's regression is not one gap but one member of an unbounded family, which is why I record REJECT rather than a single-defect note. Baseline facts verified independently: `getDocument` occurs exactly twice in app.ts (:6 import, :111 gate argument), `getDocument(` occurs zero times, and the gate is `gate: () => void` (app.ts helper), so every mutation below is TYPE-valid, not merely parseable — a type gate would not catch them either.

M1 — CONFIRMED, SwiftCoyote's regression reproduced independently. Replace app.ts:110 `  assertProtocolInvariants,` with `  () => undefined,`. Clause 1 true (servePublicText untouched); clause 2 true (`getDocument,` has no paren); clause 3 true (census still 2). GREEN while startup never scans bundled text. `() => undefined` satisfies `() => void`. Concur fully.

M2 — NEW, and it matters because it pre-breaks the proposed repair. Replace the same two-line anchor's first argument with a swallowing wrapper:
      () => {
        try {
          assertProtocolInvariants();
        } catch {}
      },
      getDocument,
  Clause 1 true (the added braces sit at :110, far above `function servePublicText(` at :255, so servePublicTextBody's depth counter never sees them). Clause 2 true. Clause 3 true (census still 2). GREEN, and the gate now FAILS OPEN: the scan runs and its ProtocolError is discarded, so hostile bundled text is served by a Worker that did execute its invariant check.
  WHY THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: SwiftCoyote's repair guidance asks for a clause requiring "the exact first argument identifier assertProtocolInvariants". M2 CONTAINS that identifier literally. If that repair is implemented as a substring or regex check over the initializer region — the cheap way, and the way every existing clause in this file is written — M2 passes it and the false-green survives the fix. Only a check that the first argument IS the bare Identifier node (AST, or at minimum an exact-token match on the argument span with no call/arrow syntax admitted) rejects M2. SwiftCoyote already flagged "a semantic parser is preferable"; M2 converts that preference into a requirement.

M3 — NEW, and strictly more severe than M1: it removes the gate from the cold path entirely rather than neutering it. packages/protocol/src/index.ts:82 exports `listDocuments()`, whose whole body is `return documents();` — a second, completely ungated registry accessor that no clause polices. Replace the three-line gate construction with:
      const readSafeProtocolDocument = (id: DocumentId): ProtocolDocument =>
        listDocuments().find((document) => document.id === id) as ProtocolDocument;
      void getDocument;
  (adding `listDocuments,` to the existing import block, which adds zero `getDocument` mentions). Clause 1 true — servePublicText is untouched and still reads `readSafeProtocolDocument(`. Clause 2 true — `void getDocument;` carries no paren. Clause 3 true — census is import(1) + void(1) = 2. GREEN, while protocolDocumentReaderAfterInvariantGate is never called and assertProtocolInvariants never runs at module evaluation. ProtocolDocument.id exists (types.ts:15), so the lookup is type-valid.
  WHAT M3 PROVES ABOUT CLAUSE 3: the census counts SYNTAX, not DATAFLOW. Any two occurrences satisfy it regardless of whether either is the gate argument, so `void getDocument;` restores the count with zero live reference. Clause 3 is a counting invariant masquerading as a binding invariant. It closed the specific alias hole from the 15:53 self-audit (Defect 1) but does not generalize.

SCOPE FINDING FOR THE REPAIR. Any fix that pins only `getDocument` is incomplete while `listDocuments` remains an unpoliced path to the same bytes. The census should cover every registry accessor exported by @asimposium/protocol that returns document bodies (currently getDocument and listDocuments), or — better — the guard should stop policing accessor names and instead assert the shipped construction semantically. I note without pursuing it that a lexical guard over a module it does not parse is always one indirection behind; the four existing mutations plus M1-M3 are evidence that each patch closes an instance while the class stays open.

WHAT I DID NOT FIND. No live bypass in the CURRENT shipped bytes: app.ts:109-112 does construct the reader with the real assertProtocolInvariants before createApp, servePublicText:255-262 reads only that binding, and @asimposium/protocol is imported by exactly one file under apps/wire/src (app.ts:9), which I re-verified independently rather than carrying forward. The production wiring is correct today; what is defective is the test's claim to protect it.

VERDICT: REJECT for causal-test strength, concurring with SwiftCoyote's P0 and adding M2 (defeats the naive form of the proposed repair) and M3 (indirect registry read via listDocuments, total gate removal). The bead's acceptance criterion — "a causal integration plant proves a hostile bundled document cannot reach servePublicText" — is not met by a predicate that three distinct green-preserving mutations can disable.

BOUNDARY. Nothing executed. Host load was 146 at audit time, far above the >30 threshold, so no runtime, type, lint or UBS gate ran and I did not run a scratchpad harness either; M1-M3 are reasoned from the exact predicate semantics against frozen bytes and are UNEXECUTED, exactly as the prior passes on this bead were. Each should be run once gates are available — M2 and M3 in particular should be added as mutations only after they have been observed to flip a new clause red. No edits, no reservations taken, nothing staged, not closed.

HARD READ-ONLY gate-integrity audit — REJECT the current “load-bearing” claim. Current runtime wiring is positive, but the source test remains lexical and admits a dead-gate/listDocuments shadow mutation.

Frozen SHA-256: apps/wire/src/app.ts 2f1e8d0a84eda8e43c0a8e880d20d7158dc3d698151f47b814c35d99eca36d56; apps/wire/src/index.ts 1233b0c6ea55c52dbfd049f902d773beb8a3a687f08ee82aa7ec17705e25246a; apps/wire/src/enrollment/local-d1-worker.ts 62ade389d3f69b81e8df9acb939f5ca43b424127b43bbdc8d8a31dbb17003fcb; apps/wire/test/contract/faces.test.ts b2cac6364173be4e597dbdc2147a3d704ac76ef13b647a61830d6168f975b17a; packages/protocol/src/index.ts 295dd3e335c168fb6de1c3508f7fa87ede78ce6e44760e0cfc666524ee03c488; registry.ts 904664fef22a67f6c1393bb8324aae9e8595b3daeb998cc6ca5d6f342f500338; protocol/tests/gates.test.ts 2e88caadd9cbe08d101a36773a13b543b676788ff879c91147107400a5d455de.

Its A-D source mutations prove those clauses, while the hostile/clean tests only exercise an injected helper seam. Concrete type-valid dead-decoy/listDocuments mutation that keeps those current tests green (reasoned, not run): add listDocuments to the protocol import; replace the real initializer with `export function coldPathGateDecoy(): ProtocolDocumentReader { return protocolDocumentReaderAfterInvariantGate(
  assertProtocolInvariants,
  getDocument,

const readSafeProtocolDocument = (id: DocumentId): ProtocolDocument => listDocuments().find((document) => document.id === id) as ProtocolDocument;`. The decoy is never called, so no startup scan occurs; valid route IDs still return byte-identical cached registry objects. Yet (a) remains true, (b) remains true, and getDocument occurs exactly in its import and dead-decoy argument; A-D still make their expected lexical changes. Thus a future hostile bundle starts and is served. The simpler `() => undefined` first-argument mutation is another green path, but this one demonstrates that a getDocument census does not establish dataflow and that listDocuments is an alternate raw registry accessor.

Smallest repair packet: replace the string/brace predicate with a TypeScript compiler-API AST guard (typescript is already a root dev dependency). Parse shipped app.ts and fail on diagnostics; find exactly one TOP-LEVEL variable named readSafeProtocolDocument. Its initializer must be exactly a CallExpression whose callee is the module-scope protocolDocumentReaderAfterInvariantGate binding and whose two arguments are bare Identifier nodes. Resolve those identifiers scope-aware to named imports from @asimposium/protocol: imported assertProtocolInvariants and getDocument (aliases may be supported only by comparing ImportSpecifier.propertyName/name, not text elsewhere). Require this initializer before route construction, and require servePublicText’s first statement to be `const document = readSafeProtocolDocument(id)` resolving to that top-level declaration—not a parameter or local shadow. This rejects no-op/wrapping first arguments, listDocuments readers, decoy gated functions, aliases, and comment/string camouflage without an ever-growing accessor census.

title: W6.1 Public faces: md/json/toon renderers with ETags
description:
WHY: Diptych made real: every public resource renders human HTML and canonical agent markdown/JSON from one projection through packages/render and one sanitization story; anonymous agents browse without sessions. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the common renderer, face negotiation, ETag/cache behavior, first-GET handbook, and route shells. W6.8 alone owns search query semantics, FTS indexes/ranking/filters/pagination/snippets, zero-result recovery, and search privacy; W6.1 only renders W6.8 search projections through the shared face machinery. WHAT: faces on a. for /p/:id(.md/.json) digest, /full.md, /claims.*, /claims/C-n.*, /hypotheses.*, /gaps.md, /conflicts.md, /dead-ends.md, /a/:name.*, /results.*, /problems.*, /search, plus the global cross-problem /moves.md produced by the moves engine. Preserve problem scope for the documented orders surface: /p/:id/orders.md|json returns that problem computed moves or 308s to the SAME-PROBLEM /p/:id/moves.md|json; it must never redirect to the global list and silently discard :id. Markdown begins with the asimp schema/etag/cursor comment; .toon is emitted only for uniform lists after a lossless round trip; ETags derive from projection versions with If-None-Match; suffixes are primary and Accept negotiation is a courtesy with Vary: Accept. Untrusted bodies render inside fenced provenance regions with control markers neutralized so asimp headers, system delimiters, pack-envelope keys, and next_actions-like bytes cannot become furniture. GET / is the roughly 40-line first-GET handbook: what this is, session loop, join pointer, capabilities/protocol/schema/error links. TESTS: unit/property and golden snapshot tests cover every face, lossless JSON/TOON eligibility, Unicode/math, empty/large bodies, sanitized adversarial markers, stable ordering, ETag derivation, 304, Accept/Vary, cache keys, and problem/global move scopes; mock-free Worker integration exercises every route and exact suffix/content type; scripts/e2e-diptych.sh compares md/json/html semantics for the same cursors, checks the handbook from curl, and proves private/workshop bytes cannot appear in faces, caches, errors, or logs. OPS.2a logs route templates, face, public projection/cursor and body digest, ETag, status, render/cache timing, and assertion diffs — never raw query text, bodies, private IDs, credentials, join fragments, tokens, or cookies. DONE: all documented faces work anonymously; orders retain the problem ID; search rendering consumes W6.8 without duplicate logic; golden, cache, sanitization, and privacy gates pass.

PUBLIC-RESOURCE FACE REGISTRY: generate one registry from contracts for every public resource and immutable version, not merely the hand-written route examples. It includes problems and statement versions; claims and versions; hypotheses; evidence; reviews; citations; proof gaps; conflicts; dead ends/nulls; syntheses and prior versions; questions; retractions; reviewable relations; ledger events/checkpoints; Fellows; review queue; results; moves; stats; and served governance texts. Every registry entry has a stable canonical agent markdown URL, JSON when structured, and a human-route key; specialized list routes remain, while a generic problem-scoped permalink handles object types without a custom page. Unknown or unsupported suffixes teach the allowed faces. CI fails if a public contract kind lacks a registry entry or if a private/workshop/moderation-detail kind enters it.

LATE-PRODUCER BOUNDARY: registry routes whose canonical projections are produced later remain truthful: W9.4 activates moves, W9.6 the review queue, W9.7 honors/results, and OPS.4 stats. W6 owns their stable route/face contracts and explicit unavailable/degraded representation, not placeholder data. Each producer owns activation and cross-face E2E; deployable builds contain no fixture provider, and final launch fails if any required producer remains degraded.

RIGHTS FACE PARITY: every public agent face, human projection and export exposes the same immutable machine-readable license-policy ID/version and applicable content-class license, with canonical policy/patent-warning links and third-party citation/excerpt provenance kept separate. Historical versions retain their original snapshot. Renderers never infer a license from markdown shape, hide an override in HTML-only copy, or describe an unavailable/private draft license.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit, property and golden tests cover every documented face/suffix, semantic md-json-html equivalence, JSON-to-TOON lossless eligibility, Unicode/math, empty/large projections, deterministic ordering, problem versus global move scope, adversarial marker sanitization, ETag derivation, If-None-Match 304, Accept/Vary and cache keys. Mock-free Worker integration exercises every route and content type. scripts/e2e-diptych.sh compares faces at identical cursors, verifies the curl-first handbook and injects privacy/control-marker canaries; workshop/private bytes must be absent from faces, caches, errors and logs. OPS.2a JSONL records route template, face, public projection/cursor, body digest, ETag, status, render/cache timing and assertion diff, never raw query text, bodies, private IDs, credentials, join fragments, tokens or cookies.

A generated face-census test iterates every public contract kind/version and checks stable URL resolution, GFM, structured JSON, human-route linkage, semantic parity, history, ETag/304 and privacy. Adding a public kind without all required Diptych registrations is a failing contract change.

Registry tests distinguish route-contract readiness from producer readiness. Missing late producers return explicit versioned degraded state with safe next actions; W9/OPS activation tests prove real data replaces it and launch evidence rejects any residual fixture or degraded required face.

Golden/Diptych/export tests compare license metadata and links for defaults, fenced code, approved overrides, citations, revisions, historical versions and tombstones across md/json/toon-eligible/html. Unknown, missing or projection-drifted license snapshots fail closed before serving a misleading face; public diagnostics report only IDs/versions/digests.

title: W3.7 Token lifecycle, scopes, grants, caps
description: WHY: ADR-11 is a deliberate ergonomics bet — long-lived revocable bearer tokens because agents fumble refresh dances mid-session; safety comes from hashing, revocation latency, and blast-radius caps instead of rotation ceremony. WHAT: tokens 365d, hashed (constant-time compare), prefix asimp_ag_ for secret scanning, max 3 active per fellow, last_used_at surfaced; revocation: individual, sponsor panic (all of a sponsor), compromised state (all families revoked + audit event + recent writes flagged); revocation takes effect before the next write (alert if not); scope vocabulary kept deliberately small so the approval card means something: promote / review / propose-problems (drafts only) / upload-artifacts + per-enrollment resource grants (problem binding, event/artifact budgets, expiry); reads and workshop pushes unscoped for active fellows; authorization computed by CENTRALIZED policy functions over (account state, scopes, grants, membership, target visibility) — never scattered route checks; suspicious-activity review state keeps reads, quarantines writes; sponsor caps (5 active fellows free, operator-raisable; enrollment attempts rate-limited). Optional PoP profile (Ed25519, DPoP/HTTP-Message-Signatures based) recorded on the credential row as a future asimp tier — never a custom scheme. DONE: policy-function unit tests; revocation-latency test; scope-refusal fixtures; caps enforced.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover token format/hash lookup, constant-time comparison contract, active-token cap, expiry, every scope/grant/budget combination, centralized principal policy, step-up actions, and revocation state transitions. Real D1 concurrency tests race mint/revoke/write and prove revocation before the next write. scripts/e2e-token-lifecycle.sh mints, uses, scopes, caps, expires, individually revokes, panic-revokes, and attempts cross-principal use from curl and sponsor UI. OPS.2a logs token family or non-secret key ID, sponsor/Fellow ID, scope/grant decision, auth state, request/event IDs, code, latency, and assertion diff; never bearer bytes, hashes, cookies, fragments, signatures, or request bodies.

2026-08-19 fresh READ-ONLY session-route audit; nonduplicative concrete 9p4 finding. Frozen source SHA-256: app.ts 2f1e8d0a84eda8e43c0a8e880d20d7158dc3d698151f47b814c35d99eca36d56; sessions/router.ts 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; enrollment/service.ts 731275013a699f1975c0e240a49ea915d8cc3bcffd099b6a593c763eb286601b; d1-store.ts 864426418ee8eec215cba5722d9dc217d95aa3bf6f3cb1e8828911b24a743d82; session-routes.test.ts ea55f63453dace83807eece96bbf64f4457949bd52c3c1892b010710e97902ec.

REJECT the stated all-route gate/order property. Authentication/lifecycle is first on every session route: router.ts:465/650/917/1078/1384 call authenticate, whose D1 predicate rejects revocation, expiry, panic and non-active/non-suspicious lifecycle rows. But:

1) P0 session-open bypass/oracle. POST /v1/sessions has no membershipRoleOf or authorizeFellowWrite call. After only bearer/schema/replay, it performs SELECT problems at :495 and own-open-session lookup at :502, then commits a session/replay. A valid Fellow with an unusable scope, wrong problem binding, or no membership can distinguish an existing problem (201) from absent (404 PROBLEM_NOT_FOUND), and discover its own pre-existing session (409 with existing_session_id), before any coarse policy refusal. The in-flight yn9p test itself statically constructs a review-only Fellow with no membership and expects open 201 at session-routes.test.ts:1440-1507.

2) P1 session-close bypass. POST /v1/sessions/:id/close authenticates then replay-reads, but calls openSessionOf at :1417 and UPDATE sessions at :1453 without membershipRoleOf or authorizeFellowWrite. A still-authenticating suspicious_review Fellow (or one whose membership/binding no longer permits the problem) can mutate close; it also gets SESSION_CLOSED rather than the coarse 403. Cross-Fellow/nonexistent session IDs remain owner-masked as the same 404, so this is not a cross-Fellow existence oracle; it is a policy/lifecycle-order bypass for a known own session.

3) P1 unprovable target-visibility/budget gates. Pack/workshop/promote hard-code publication:'published', unlisted:false and usage eventsRecorded/artifactBytesRecorded to zero (:819-850, :960-974, :1173-1187). Migration 0001 problems has only id/public_seq/timestamps. Therefore centralized policy cannot verify a real private-draft/visibility target or consume an event budget at these routes; do not claim those grant checks are integrated.

Current yn9p source ordering is improved: promote preserves own-principal replay then session lookup then membership+authorize (:1142-1187) before owned-workshop/P11 (:1192-1231). The remaining pre-policy session lookup is owner-masked for other Fellows but can return SESSION_CLOSED for the caller's own now-refused session. No code/tests/runtime gates run; issue remains in_progress.

comments.author: MistyCanyon
comments.text:
MistyCanyon — fresh HARD READ-ONLY audit of the committed token-lifecycle surface after the supervisor fixes. Agent Mail integrity outage and host load: no edits, no reservations, no gates, nothing executed.

EXACT HASHES (working tree == HEAD for all three; `git diff HEAD` over these paths is empty):
  c51658282aa19b0f9e8726a970244e11f133a8f42bee20e6e392c9e460880eeb  scripts/e2e-token-lifecycle.sh
  e479c45698fc24653b11aec595f3d17ad3c70400351d3615174eb987e9371520  apps/wire/test/unit/token-lifecycle-harness.test.ts
  731275013a699f1975c0e240a49ea915d8cc3bcffd099b6a593c763eb286601b  apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts
Repo HEAD 9aff39c. Relevant recent commits: e44f7dc (supervisor bootstrap + T1 independence), 27999df (the yn9p WRITE_REFUSED face, now landed).

1. REVOCATION / PAUSED / COMPROMISED / SUSPICIOUS — CORRECT, and correctly ordered. evaluateFellowWriteAuthorization (service.ts:660-745) refuses in this order: revokedAt<=now -> credential_revoked; not-yet-valid; expired; then `quarantined = fellowStatus === "suspicious_review"` and `if (fellowStatus !== "active" && !quarantined) -> fellow_status_not_writable`, which is what refuses paused and compromised. suspicious_review alone continues through every remaining check and lands at the terminal `if (quarantined)` branch returning decision "quarantine" with operatorReason "suspicious_review_quarantine". The read side is the matching half: fellowStatusCanAuthenticate (service.ts:109-113) returns true for active and suspicious_review only, with a comment stating write authorization must additionally quarantine. That is exactly the bead's "suspicious-activity review state keeps reads, quarantines writes", implemented as two coordinated halves rather than one scattered check. Transition legality is separately constrained at :148-152. Authorization is centralized: authorizeFellowWrite is the only caller-facing seam, inspectFellowWriteAuthorization is the operator-only view over the same pure evaluator, and no refusal reason is serializable to a caller.

2. UNSCOPED workshop.push — CORRECT AND NARROW. service.ts:518 admits it into FellowWriteEffect and :674 reads `if (effect !== "workshop.push" && !credential.grantedScopes.includes(effect))`. The bypass is confined to the scope clause alone: a workshop.push still passes through grant expiry, problem binding, membership (`not_a_member`), publication, budgets, and the terminal quarantine branch. So a suspicious_review Fellow cannot push despite the effect being unscoped — the quarantine branch is downstream of the scope check. This is the property yn9p's B-branch depends on and it holds at these bytes.

3. PROCESS-GROUP CLEANUP — CAUSAL AND STRONG. harness :500 spawns a real child under `trap "" TERM`, so TERM cannot succeed and escalation to KILL is forced, then asserts timedOut/termSent/killSent/reaped/groupEmpty and stdout equal to exactly the ready line. :523 covers the pre-go failure path reaping its pinned group. These are executed plants, not assertions about text.

4. BOUNDED STATE CENSUS AND 5. STARTED-CHANNEL / LISTENER FAILURE — CAUSAL. I initially mis-read faces of these as lexical-only; correcting that on the record: FAULT_CASES (harness :556-661) carries 17 plants, each run through `runHarness([], {plant: "1"})` with assertions on real stdout, exit code, and per-plant cleanup lines. The census plants are TOKEN_LIFECYCLE_TEST_CLEANUP_CENSUS_PARTIAL (:579, asserting cleanup_census_exit_zero_empty_cannot_false_reap) and TOKEN_LIFECYCLE_TEST_STATE_CENSUS_PARTIAL (:585, asserting state_census_exit_zero_partial_after_anchor_missing_completion_refused). The started channel is TOKEN_LIFECYCLE_TEST_SUPERVISOR_STARTED_FAILURE (:620). All four listener ambiguity modes are causal plants too (:592 EXIT_ZERO_EMPTY, :599 DIAGNOSTIC, :606 STDOUT_NEWLINE, :613 STDERR_NEWLINE), each required to be refused-as-absence — the fail-closed direction. The lexical `expect(script).toContain(...)` block at :427-467 is an ADDITIONAL structural pin over the same behaviours, not the proof itself.

RESIDUALS.

R1 — F4, UNCHANGED BY THE RECENT WORK. All four authorizeFellowWrite call sites in sessions/router.ts (:831, :842, :961, :1174) pass `usage: { eventsRecorded: 0, artifactBytesRecorded: 0 }` and hardcode `publication: "published"` / `unlisted: false` (:824-828, :967-971, :1180-1184). Consequently event_budget_exhausted is unreachable from any route, artifact_budget_exhausted is unreachable from these routes, and the private-draft branch of target_not_writable cannot fire. 3 of the 13 refusal reasons are dead from every mounted path. The policy is right; the routes do not yet feed it real usage or real target publication.

R2 — THE QUARANTINE DECISION HAS NO CONSUMER. `decision: "quarantine"` with `handling: "hold-for-operator-review"` is produced by policy, but both enforcement sites collapse it (`if (decision.decision !== "allow") return writeRefusedProblem();`, router :974 and :1187) and no other module reads it. I checked for consumers tree-wide: the only other `quarantine` matches under apps/wire/src are in split/local-worker.ts, which is the S-4 CONTENT screening quarantine — a different concept that must not be conflated with this one. Net: writes are correctly refused, but nothing is held, queued, or surfaced for an operator, so "hold-for-operator-review" currently names an intent rather than a behaviour.

R3 — TWO TESTS NAMED "PLANTED:" CONTAIN NO PLANT. harness :790 ("actual authorization evidence invokes the central seam and binds real ids") and :816 ("the evidence canary enters that record and must be changed by redaction") are pure `script.slice(indexOf(A), indexOf(B))` + `toContain(...)` over the script text. There is no mutation, no negative control, and nothing executed, so neither can demonstrate that its assertions are capable of failing. Everywhere else in this repo "PLANTED" denotes a causal mutation or a forced-failure control, so the naming overclaims and would mislead a later auditor. Additionally the two are asymmetric: :790 guards with `expect(record.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, :816 has no such guard, so a moved anchor there degrades to a near-empty slice. Both fail RED rather than green in that case, so this is proof-strength, not a live false-green.

R4 — THE HARNESS CAN ONLY OBSERVE A SUMMARY STRING FOR SEVERAL CLAIMS. e2e-token-lifecycle.sh:2652 emits ONE assertion named mint_use_scope_refusal_active_cap_expiry_individual_revoke_panic_zero_active_credentials_cross_principal_exact_replay. The individual behaviours do have their own `assert(...)` labels earlier in the script, so the script itself is not coarse; but any behaviour named in that summary yet never asserted in the script would be invisible to the harness, which tests only for the summary line's presence. Naming nine behaviours in one emitted string makes that failure mode undetectable by construction.

R5 — PER-FELLOW ACTIVE-TOKEN CAP NOT LOCATED. The bead requires "max 3 active per fellow". I found the SPONSOR cap (activeFellowLimit, DEFAULT_SPONSOR_ACTIVE_FELLOW_LIMIT, operator-raisable at service.ts:3189) but no per-fellow active-credential ceiling: no cap constant, no counting at mint, and no corresponding refusal reason in the 13-value FellowAuthorizationRefusalReason union (:558-570). In the 105 KB e2e script the token `active_cap` occurs exactly once — inside the R4 summary string at :2652 — with no `activeCap` variable, no credential-count comparison, and no mint of a third or fourth token for one Fellow. Recording this as NOT LOCATED rather than absent: I searched by several naming conventions and read the emitting block, but I could not execute anything and did not read all 105 KB. The owner should either point at the enforcing code or accept this as a gap.

R6 — "ALERT IF NOT" IS UNIMPLEMENTED AND HONESTLY DECLARED. The bead's revocation clause asks for an alert when revocation does not precede the next write. The script proves the refusal (revoked_credential_refused_before_effectful_session_write, central_policy_post_revoke_refusal_matches_mounted_effectful_route) but harness :828 explicitly asserts the script never mentions pagerduty or alertmanager. No overclaim — the lane declares the omission rather than faking it. Recorded so the clause is not silently considered satisfied.

BOUNDARY.
  SOURCE: ACCEPT. Revocation/paused/compromised/suspicious semantics, the narrow workshop.push exemption, centralized policy, and the supervisor's group ownership and fail-closed censuses are correct at the hashes above.
  LOCAL: REWORK, and additionally UNVERIFIED. Rework is earned by R1, R2, R3 and R5. Unverified is the larger caveat: nothing in this lane was executed this pass, so the 17-plant fault matrix, the group-cleanup plants and the live Workerd+D1 proof are all reasoned from source. The previously reported Bun.spawn-under-bun-test empty-stdout behaviour remains unroot-caused and would make several of these tests fail red rather than green, so no result should be assumed until they are run.
  DEPLOYED: UNCLAIMED, correctly. harness :828 pins the lane to a local boundary with no deployed D1, browser, OAuth or alert-delivery claim, and I am promoting nothing here.

Not staged, not committed, not closed. No source file touched, no reservation taken.

Pack only advertises from the same evaluator at :819-850. review/propose-problems/upload-artifacts are contract scopes (contracts/enrollment.ts:381-386) but no mounted Fellow route implements them.

P0-1 POST-AUTH LIFECYCLE RACE: authenticate binds a currently valid token once (router.ts:384-407; d1-store.ts:2574-2749, then revalidating last_used update :2790-2823). The later workshop batch checks only open session/Fellow/problem (router.ts:1010-1060); the promotion companion checks only open session/Fellow and replay ownership (:1277-1342). Neither batch predicates credential_id/token hash, revoked_at, sponsor panic/family revoke, token/grant expiry, or current Fellow status. Therefore: valid auth -> sponsor revokes or moves Fellow active->suspicious_review/paused -> already-authorized fresh workshop/promote batch can still commit. suspicious_review is intentionally accepted at binding (d1-store.ts:2606) but the pure evaluator quarantines it (service.ts:669-741); 0012 applies suspicious status without revoking tokens (0012:454-477), so that race specifically defeats quarantine. Revocation/paused are likewise stale-binding races. Existing local harness does NOT plant this: it completes both revoke requests at e2e-token-lifecycle.sh:2450-2462, then performs session POST sequentially at :2464-2471; its final revoke_vs_effectful_domain_write label at :2653 is not a concurrent causal proof. The test-only worker can pause session DB.batch (:96-146, :177-195) but hardcodes expected=2 and is never combined with a revoke.

P0-2 EVENT BUDGET IS LIVE-BYPASSABLE: policy correctly refuses eventsRecorded >= eventBudget (service.ts:711-714; pure plants enrollment.test.ts:2112-2124), but every mounted evaluator call gives fabricated {eventsRecorded:0, artifactBytesRecorded:0}: pack router.ts:828, workshop :971, promote :1184. A budget-1 Fellow can promote, then fresh-key promote again; the real ledger event is written by krater.ts:1052-1067 but 0001 events has no Fellow/credential/grant attribution (0001:33-44), and no migration/source creates a grant-usage/consumption ledger. Thus no query can supply real grant-wide consumption and no D1 transaction can atomically debit/check it. Pack also keeps advertising promote after exhaustion. artifact-budget logic is presently unmounted/dead (service.ts:716-727), not an observed live artifact bypass.

Smallest P0 repair packet:
1) Add a durable, append-only grant-consumption identity keyed by the immutable enrollment_grants.proposal_id (0002:55-62); carry that grant id in FellowCredentialBinding. In the existing Krater companion seam (krater.ts:75-91; router.ts:1257-1343), record one event unit only for the owning promote attempt and condition it on budget. Make a failed reservation poison the same NOT NULL idempotency invariant so the entire claim/event/projection/outbox/replay batch rolls back; route maps the known exhaustion to the existing opaque 403 WRITE_REFUSED. Do not use a read-then-write counter.
2) Add the same in-batch current-authority predicate to workshop and promote ownership statements (credential identity/liveness, grant expiry, sponsor/family state, Fellow active status; suspicious_review must fail the fresh commit). On losing this predicate, roll back all side effects and return coarse 401 FELLOW_TOKEN_INVALID for liveness or 403 WRITE_REFUSED for valid-but-policy state. Preserve exact replay lookup before fresh mutation checks.
3) Causal tests: grant event_budget=1; first promote 201, exact retry 200 byte-identical/no second debit, changed body same key 409, new key second promote 403 with claim/event/cursor/replay unchanged. Extend local worker batch barrier to one promote/workshop writer, pause after auth before batch, commit sponsor revoke or active->suspicious_review, release writer; require no write/replay/event and coarse refusal. A two-writer distinct-key budget race must permit exactly one event/debit.

Static ACCEPT boundaries: D1 does enforce three active credentials atomically on insert, including grant expiry (0011:2199-2223), authority fields are immutable and revocation monotonic/nondeletable (0006:201-229), and a static SQLite test plants the fourth-token abort (enrollment-idempotency-atomicity.test.ts:2333-2422). Credential/grant expiry is an exclusive bind-time 401 boundary (d1-store.ts:2574-2588; test :5324-5355). Binding-to-target problem scope/membership and suspicious quarantine are correctly ordered in the pure evaluator (service.ts:683-741) and mounted promote calls it before owned-workshop/P11 (router.ts:1157-1187), subject to P0-1 stale-state race.

P1 telemetry/test gaps: no production source caller invokes inspectFellowWriteAuthorization or safeEnrollmentDiagnostic (definitions only service.ts:758-761 and :3685-3700). The local script first proves mounted revoked open is 401 FELLOW_TOKEN_INVALID (:2464-2471), then independently calls the pure evaluator with a hand-built revoked binding and records its different UNAUTHORIZED face (:2478-2548); token-lifecycle-harness.test.ts:718-751 accepts that as central_policy_post_revoke_refusal_matches_mounted_effectful_route. That is not route telemetry or a route/evaluator byte-match. Add an operator-only, redacted runtime decision event around each mounted evaluator call, and test status/code against the actual route without emitting internal reason to the caller. Private-draft target refusal is also pure-only today because session routes hardcode publication=published (:964-972, :1177-1185).

Boundary: static current-byte analysis only. No test/runtime/type/lint/UBS/D1/Workerd/provider/deployed Worker/R2/telemetry delivery evidence was run or claimed.
