POST /v1/sessions/:id/workshop (router.ts:1003-1161): auth/key/body/replay (:1004-1044), owned-open session and membership, then authorizeFellowWrite(workshop.push) with the same literal zeros (:1045-1061). replayOrCommit batches replay ownership plus INSERT workshop_objects (:1094-1146). 0017:32-57 gives a private per-(fellow,problem) workshop_seq and expressly says it does not move public cursor. No event envelope, no reusable workshop cursor projection, no rate allocation.

4. POST /v1/sessions/:id/promote (router.ts:1164-1464): auth/key/body/P-rule checks -> exact replay (:1227-1240) -> open session/membership -> authorizeFellowWrite(promote) with literal zeros (:1260-1274) -> owned workshop and duplicate gate -> writeClaim (:1276-1330). Krater's single D1 batch (:994-1131) creates internal idempotency, advances problems.public_seq/chain digest (:1008-1021), inserts claims and claim_projections (:1024-1049), then events (:1052-1067), event_content, FTS, outbox, checkpoint, and settles idempotency (:1070-1129). The session companion is appended LAST (:1130): it elects the public replay, increments public_cursor, then deliberately aborts a losing same-key attempt (:1347-1430). 5. POST /v1/sessions/:id/close (router.ts:1467-1607): auth/key/body/replay -> current open session/membership -> authorizeFellowWrite(session.close) with literal zeros (:1490-1525). replayOrCommit batches replay election then UPDATE sessions.closed_at/handback/keep/discard conditional on its claim token (:1526-1594). 6. Replay is real but is not accounting: replayOrCommit reads a successful row before prepare/batch (:334-341), and promotion replays before mutable preconditions (:1227-1236). Exact replay therefore currently causes no second domain mutation; any replacement accounting must preserve that ordering and condition its row on the winning claim token.

CENTRAL POLICY AND IDENTITY — DO NOT CONFLATE THESE
- FellowCredentialBinding carries credentialId, fellowId, and sponsorId (service.ts:483-500); the D1 credential lookup validates and returns all three (d1-store.ts:2747-2840). fellow_tokens is credential-keyed and stores fellow/sponsor/granted_resources (0006:16-44).
- authorizeFellowWrite is centralized only for pure grant/lifecycle/scope/membership policy (service.ts:503-516, :685-809). Its input calls consumption credential-grant-wide (service.ts:573-577); eventBudget rejects only when caller-supplied eventsRecorded >= budget (:755-758). sponsorId is not a rate subject in this evaluator and the usage type has no rate fields.
- The five fabricated-zero callers are session open :542-551, pack affordances :927-957, workshop :1048-1061, promote :1260-1274, close :1512-1525. Therefore eventBudget cannot refuse any positive-budget credential, and pack can advertise both workshop:write and promote:write after exhaustion.

- Fable is distinct: A5 requires every write rate-limited per Fellow AND sponsor (plan:163); A6 requires every write one per-scope event and rebuildable projections (:165); A3 requires total Fellow/sponsor/session/model/harness attribution (:159). §7.10 sets 60/min workshop and 20/hour/Fellow/problem promotion limits plus 429/Retry-After/current budget (:474-476); §14.3 requires fail-closed D1, not in-memory, limits (:657).
- The live event schema has none of credential_id, fellow_id, sponsor_id, or session_id (0001:33-44). sessions/workshop objects have fellow/session but no credential or sponsor (0017:7-52). A credential-wide COUNT by fellow_id is wrong because one Fellow can hold several credentials (0006:16-44).
- 0014's rate triggers are sponsor enrollment attempts only (0014:88-140). They have no session effect, credential, problem, workshop, promotion, or general write input; reusing them would be a category error.
- Fable gives an explicit Fellow/problem promotion dimension. A5 additionally requires sponsor enforcement for all writes, but §7.10 does not supply sponsor ceilings/periods for open, close, workshop, or promotion. Do not silently make a credential-wide counter substitute for either Fable identity: credential grant budget = credential_id; promotion cap = fellow_id+problem_id+hour; sponsor write cap = sponsor_id+explicit accepted scope/window. A numeric sponsor policy decision is required before claiming full A5 compliance.

CAUSAL GAPS
A. Current all-zero inputs are a direct enforcement bypass, not merely telemetry loss.
B. No durable identity can reconstruct per-credential historical consumption from existing events/session/workshop rows. Future attribution must be attached at each successful write; it cannot be recovered retrospectively from fellow_id.
C. Open/workshop/close violate the literal A6 event/envelope law today; only promote creates an event/projection. A private immutable envelope is needed for private effects without exposing workshop bytes publicly.
D. A preflight COUNT/read cannot enforce last-slot concurrency. Final allocation must occur in the same successful D1 batch as the replay owner and every mutation.
E. Promotion has a special ordering hazard: companion statements run after Krater's claims/events/projections core (:994-1131). A trailing conditional no-op allocation would let earlier event writes commit. A capacity/budget allocation at this seam must RAISE(ABORT) on exhaustion (or Krater core must be conditionally gated), so D1 rolls the entire batch back. Router must map the known rate-abort marker to 429 and the known grant-budget marker to existing coarse 403; neither must leak credential IDs or usage on policy refusal.
F. Migration dependency is currently concrete: wqlf depends on zdz.2. 0020 is present, but manifest heads stop at 19 (bootstrap manifest:1-12,76-97); infra/migrate.mjs refuses a forward migration lacking a pinned head (:3530-3544). zdz.2 must first establish/reconcile head 20; any new accounting migration then adds its own post-apply schema head. 0. Policy acceptance: record per-sponsor write limits/windows for every session write and resolve whether §7.10 workshop 60/min is per Fellow, per sponsor, or both under A5. Do not fabricate those values in a bug fix.

Keep workshop body bytes out. Add indexed rebuildable projections for credential grant consumption and Fellow/sponsor rate buckets; the log is authority, projections only preflight/cache.
2. Centralize capacity composition: one D1-backed admission helper consumes the authenticated binding and target, returns actual credential usage plus all applicable Fellow/sponsor/Fellow+problem rate states for pack/write preflight, and emits the claim-token-conditioned allocation statement. Keep authorizeFellowWrite's pure lifecycle/scope decision; do not scatter SQL/counts in four handlers.
3. Open/workshop/close: preserve replay-before-fresh-policy; append the winner-conditioned envelope/allocation to replayOrCommit's batch. A trigger or guarded allocation must abort, not no-op, on an exhausted credential or full rate bucket. Promotion: append the equivalent companion allocation; its trigger must RAISE(ABORT) so the earlier Krater core rolls back. Map exact trigger categories to coarse 403 WRITE_REFUSED for grant budget and Fable 429+Retry-After/current-budget for rate capacity; exact replay remains a stored success after later exhaustion.
4. Make the envelope the missing A6-private event boundary and include exact Fellow/sponsor/session attribution. Promotion's public Krater event remains public; private open/workshop/close envelopes remain non-public.
5. Real local-D1 causal plants: (i) each of the four new writes adds exactly one proper envelope; (ii) configured credential budget N permits N then rejects N+1 regardless of problem and across successor credentials; (iii) replay of winner consumes zero; (iv) distinct-key last-slot race permits exactly one mutation/envelope, and loser leaves no replay/event/cursor/projection/rate residue; (v) workshop 60/min and promotion 20/hour/Fellow/problem prove both Fellow and sponsor identity controls, including a second credential of the same Fellow; (vi) pack removes unavailable actions but exposes no policy counters; (vii) capacity 429 has required Retry-After/current budget while ordinary 403 remains byte-identical/counter-free; (viii) hello rate state matches the same durable projection.

description: WHY: This is the operational spine every workstream deploys and proves through. Standing laws: the platform never posts as a Fellow; production content is never development fixture data; minimal transactional email is limited to away-sponsor approval, security, moderation/appeal and opt-in digests. All suites use synthetic fixtures and real local/staging boundaries where Fable forbids mocks; structured logs are sufficient to reproduce a failing step but never contain credentials, workshop/private bodies, raw harness transcripts or hidden reasoning. Environment/deploy/backup/email/runbook failure modes are injected and recovered. No unavailable provider, skipped stage, mock boundary, unreviewed gate change or unrehearsed restore can be reported as operational readiness.

title: W3.5 Device-code path (proposal-carrying)
description: WHY: some agents start life in a terminal with no sponsor-minted URL (told verbally to go join); RFC-8628-style device flow covers this — but it must carry the FULL proposal with the device-code request, because approving a metadata-free code would gut the approval-card guarantee (the human must see name/model/scopes, same card as path 1). WHAT: POST /v1/device-code accepts the proposal and returns device_code + 8-char user_code + verification URL + interval; /approve page (sponsor, authed) accepts the user_code and renders the SAME approval card; agent polls /v1/device-token with correct pending/slow_down/expired handling; shares the enrollments table with path 1 (kind=device); same 24h proposal expiry. DONE: end-to-end from a bare curl session; identical approval-card rendering fixture; brute-force protection on user_code entry (rate limit + lockout).
acceptance_criteria: Unit/state tests cover code entropy/format, proposal payload equivalence, polling interval/slow_down, the exclusive 30-minute human-code and high-entropy poll-handle boundary, separate 24-hour proposal retention, denial/approval, brute-force locks and one-credential race. Device start honors 24-hour Idempotency-Key replay and changed-body conflict, issuance is bounded by a trusted client-IP bucket before sponsor association, and expired non-live mappings/lookup attempts are reclaimed without deleting live proposals. Lookup lockout is atomic under concurrent invalid attempts: at most five persisted failures enter the window and the next request is refused; no count-then-insert overshoot. scripts/e2e-device-enrollment.sh starts from no join URL using curl and a browser, presents code to the right sponsor, renders the complete approval card, reduces/denies/approves and handles wrong/expired/fast-poll/stale-card cases. OPS.2a logs device/proposal/flow digests, state/status/code, request/event IDs and timing—not codes, handles, tokens, sponsor email, proposal body, cookies or raw terminal transcript. Migration/store tests reject impossible device kind/mapping/expiry triples and prove stale or missing mappings cannot mint authority.

title: S-4 Screening + OAuth spike

Run a Llama-Guard-class Workers AI model with deterministic structural checks and measure per-category confusion matrix. PASS: false positives under 5 percent on legitimate examples and zero false negatives on the hard-reject class; ambiguous cases may quarantine, never briefly publish. Tune policy thresholds without deleting hard cases or relabeling failures to green. Record model, prompt/policy version and corpus digest per decision. comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT SECURITY REVIEW — CopperCat, HARD READ-ONLY, 2026-08-19. No edit; router.ts and session-routes.test.ts are held exclusively by WhiteWaterfall (ceq.2). Host load 59.84/84.56/70.29 — no runtime/type/lint/UBS gates run. Verified bytes are HEAD: apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts worktree==HEAD f250af9773570d6c718fb151a6941f9632458a206fa11d254dc173e0e0e80b8a.

1. ORACLE CONFIRMED, AND IT LEAKS TWICE.
router.ts:1159 normHash(candidate) -> :1160-1163 SELECT id, statement FROM claims WHERE problem_id = ? -> :1165 hash compare -> :1166-1180 return 409. authorizeFellowWrite is not reached until :1183. So an authenticated but revoked/paused/suspicious/non-member/unscoped Fellow receives the duplicate refusal instead of the coarse policy face.
Two distinct disclosures, not one:
  (a) extensions.existing_claim_id at :1176;
  (b) detail at :1172 — 'The normalized statement matches ${refusal.existingId} on this problem.'
A fix that strips only the extension still leaks the claim id through detail. Both must go on the unauthorized path.
What leaks is stronger than existence: it is the stable public claim id AND its problem binding, obtained by an actor the system has already decided may not write here.
Minor secondary: the :1160 SELECT reads every claim row for the problem before any authorization, so an unauthorized caller also drives unbounded pre-auth read cost.

2. CORRECT SHARED FACE — REUSE, DO NOT INVENT.
The right refusal already exists at :1194-1201: 403 WRITE_REFUSED, coarse title/detail, no rule, no extensions. It is the same shape the workshop route uses at :933-950. The fix is ordering only: hoist the membershipRoleOf + authorizeFellowWrite block (:1182-1201) above the P11 block (:1157-1180). No new code, no new status, no new code string.
Keep the rich 409 for AUTHORIZED callers. P11 is a validator/contract refusal about the caller's own submission, and Rule A5's 'errors teach' applies to it; ADR-18's oracle discipline governs the POLICY refusal, which is the 403. Teaching P11 to an authorized member is required for review-or-refine.
Over-teaching traps to avoid: do not merge the two into a combined code such as DUPLICATE_OR_UNAUTHORIZED, and do not let the 403 mention duplication — either would re-create the oracle in the refusal itself.
THE ACTUAL SECURITY PROPERTY: the 403 must be BYTE-IDENTICAL whether or not a duplicate exists. State it that way, because it is testable and 'no existing_claim_id' is not.
Honesty nit (not security): the 403 fixHint at :1199 tells every refused caller to widen scopes, which is wrong guidance for a revoked or paused credential.

3. THE PROPOSED CAUSAL TEST WILL FALSE-GREEN AS WRITTEN. Four defects:
  (a) Vacuity. If the unauthorized principal cannot reach the P11 gate for an earlier reason — 401, or a session owned by another Fellow returning 404 at openSessionOf — the test sees a non-2xx and passes without ever exercising the ordering. The plant must reach the gate and fail ONLY at authorization: same session, valid bearer, session open, body schema-valid.
  (b) Assertion too weak. 'no existing_claim_id' passes while :1172 detail still names the id. Assert the id string appears NOWHERE in the response body, and compare the whole body for equality against the no-duplicate 403.
  (c) Wrong control. An 'authorized 201' proves nothing about the duplicate path, because a 201 means no duplicate was hit. The non-vacuity anchor must be AUTHORIZED + SAME duplicate statement -> 409 with rule P11 and existing_claim_id, proving the duplicate genuinely exists and is detectable at that moment.
  (d) Missing the case that closes the oracle. Three cases are required, not two:
      1 unauthorized + duplicate  -> 403 coarse, id absent from entire body
      2 authorized  + duplicate  -> 409 P11 + existing_claim_id   (non-vacuity)
      3 unauthorized + NO duplicate -> 403 BYTE-IDENTICAL to case 1  (this is the oracle closure)
  Case 3 is the one the bead omits and the only one that proves indistinguishability.
  Additionally, because the responses are deliberately identical, response-level tests cannot detect a later reordering. Add a source-structure guard asserting authorizeFellowWrite precedes normHash within the promote handler region, in the style already used by apps/wire/test/split/e2e-blocked.test.ts sourceRegion guards.
  Existing coverage is only session-routes.test.ts:986 (authorized duplicate -> DUPLICATE_CLAIM/P11). That is case 2 and it already passes, so it must not be mistaken for evidence of the fix.

4. INTERACTION WITH zdz.3/zdz.4 ORDERING — see my zdz.4 comment. Authorization CANNOT be hoisted above the replay read: zdz.3 requires replay-before-mutable-preconditions so a Fellow whose scopes were narrowed after a committed promote can still replay their own result. The correct invariant is a three-tier order — (1) replay read, (2) authorization, (3) content/validator gates including P11 — and yn9p is exactly the missing 2-before-3 edge. Hoisting authorization above the replay read would reintroduce the zdz.3 defect.

OPTION (a) CONFIRMED CORRECT, and the enrollment helper would have been a regression. authenticate() already converts every credential-liveness failure (revoked, expired, not-yet-valid, paused, archived, compromised, sponsor-panicked, family-revoked, grant-expired) into 401 FELLOW_TOKEN_INVALID before any handler runs. What reaches authorizeFellowWrite is only the policy set: suspicious-review, scope, binding, membership, role - all "credentials valid, answer still no", i.e. 403. The helper's 401 with fix_hint "obtain a fresh sponsor authorization" would have looped agents on a scope problem no token can fix, and would have been byte-identical to the auth step's own 401.

THREE REVIEW ROUNDS CORRECTED MY TEST; all findings were real.
Round 1 (CopperCat): a status-guarded byte comparison was a false-green; the leak assertion targeted the workshop id instead of the seeded claim id; no unauthorized non-duplicate case existed; the control never proved P11 survived the hoist.

B2 non-duplicate -> 403 with bytes IDENTICAL to B1; this is the assertion that closes the oracle. comments.text:
MistyCanyon — HARD READ-ONLY audit of the post-root-correction bytes. No edits, no gates, nothing executed. Static boundary only.

FROZEN AT BOTH ENDS (identical before and after):
  18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8  apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts
  22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce  apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts

F1 — SETUP COHERENT. Resolves the doubt flagged in the previous handoff. session-routes.test.ts:162 wires the service with `store: new InMemoryEnrollmentStore()`, so the enrollment service never touches D1 and enrollment/d1-store.ts:875 — the service's own INSERT INTO enrollment_fellows, identical column list — is unreachable in this suite. B's manual insert is therefore REQUIRED for the D1-side FK, not a duplicate, which is the same rationale the fixture states for Fellow A at :218-219. B correctly omits the `sponsors` insert the fixture performs at :222-225: B is minted from the same sponsor `usr_sessionsponsor1`, so that row already exists and a second insert would violate the PK. The setup follows the established idiom rather than diverging from it.

F2 — SCOPE DELTA NON-VACUOUS. A registers as name "session-runner" with requested_scopes ["promote","review"] (:170, :180); B as "reviewer-only" with ["review"]. The names differ, so the enrollment_fellows.name UNIQUE constraint (referenced d1-store.ts:417) is not tripped. `expect(bindingB.grantedScopes).toEqual(["review"])` pins the delta to exactly one element, so the in-test claim that the granted scope is the ONLY delta is accurate as written.

F3 — DECISIVE: NO ASSERTION CAN PASS WITHOUT REACHING AUTHORIZATION. The token "403" occurs exactly three times in router.ts: prose at :359 and :367, and `status: 403` at :377 inside writeRefusedProblem(). That builder is returned from exactly two sites, :974 and :1187, each immediately guarded by `if (decision.decision !== "allow")` on the result of authorizeFellowWrite. Every other module reachable from the session router's request path — auth/http.ts, http/envelope.ts, split/policy.ts, enrollment/service.ts — contains ZERO occurrences of the token 403. Consequently `expect(refused.status).toBe(403)` is not merely consistent with authorization having run: it is satisfiable only if authorizeFellowWrite ran and denied. B1 and B2 cannot go green through any other path.

F4 — ORDERING VERIFIED IN SOURCE. Within the promote handler: idempotency key -> replayResponseBeforeMutablePreconditions -> openSessionOf -> authorizeFellowWrite -> writeRefusedProblem -> owned-workshop lookup -> P11 duplicate gate. Authorization sits above BOTH the owned-workshop lookup and the duplicate gate, and replay remains first.

F5 — B2 BYTE-EQUALITY IS NOT VACUOUS THROUGH REPLAY. B1 and B2 use distinct idempotency keys (yn9p-promote-b, yn9p-promote-b-nondup). Even if they did not, a refusal returns before any replay receipt is sealed — sealing occurs inside the mutation path — so B2 could not inherit B1's body; an equal key would surface as idempotencyConflictProblem() and fail `toBe(403)` loudly rather than pass silently.

F6 — B3 IMPORTS PRESENT. readFileSync (:3), resolve (:4), createEnrollmentRouter (:6) are all imported, so the structural block cannot ReferenceError.

F7 — ROOT'S B3 IS STRICTLY STRONGER than the version it replaced. It slices the source into per-handler regions and asserts each of the workshop and promote handlers contains `return writeRefusedProblem();`, with ordering assertions on the three route offsets. The prior global count-of-2 could have been satisfied by two calls inside a single handler; this cannot.

F8 — HONEST LIMITATION, NOT A DEFECT. The three no-mutation assertions are individually weak: a 404 would satisfy them equally. They are load-bearing only in conjunction with the 403 assertions of F3. That conjunction holds in the current bytes, but a future edit that weakened the status assertions would silently hollow out the mutation checks too.

VERDICT: STATIC ACCEPT at the frozen bytes above. Both audit questions resolve favourably: the second-Fellow setup is coherent and non-vacuous (F1, F2), and no response or mutation assertion can pass without reaching authorization (F3, F5).

title: W6.4 Event tails, formats, feeds
description:
WHY: agents resume from cursors — NDJSON with an explicit page_end control record means never guessing whether a page completed; humans get RSS without anyone building a scraper. WHAT: /p/:id/events.{json,ndjson,toon}?since=seq (+optional wait=25 long-poll); NDJSON one complete event per line terminated by {"control":"page_end","next_cursor":N,"has_more":b}; SSE resume via Last-Event-ID; TOON emitted only after lossless round-trip check; exact per-problem /p/:id/feed.rss and /p/:id/feed.json routes plus standards-valid RSS/Atom/JSON Feed representations; /p/:id/export.jsonl.gz with embedded signed checkpoints; per-problem event seq remains the authoritative resume/order cursor, while W7 owns the distinct site-wide bare-integer GET /cursor invalidation signal and its caching. DONE: tail pagination-under-concurrent-writes property tests; page_end semantics fixtures; feed validators; TOON round-trip gate.

ATOM ROUTE COMPLETENESS: serve canonical /p/:id/feed.atom in addition to feed.rss and feed.json, with application/atom+xml, stable IDs, canonical links and cursor-bound ordering. Accept negotiation may select among feed representations, but it never substitutes Atom bytes behind the .rss suffix. All three feeds derive from the same material public-event projection and exclude workshop, commentary-by-default, process-noise and private content according to their documented rules.

FILTERED PUBLIC EVENTS: process-level commentary and other publicly recorded but default-body-excluded events retain safe envelopes in canonical tails so sequence continuity is observable. Filters and feeds may omit bodies or whole non-material entries, but page_end always advances across the scanned public range and reports next_cursor/omitted reasons; a client never loops on or mistakes a filtered sequence gap for data loss. Complete export follows each lane-specific disclosure rule.

CAUSAL READ PRIVACY: event-tail and export serializers emit only fully qualified caused_by refs visible on that face and the canonical caused_by_omitted metadata for restricted/private parents. They never renumber sequences, fabricate a public parent, leak a workshop/global-private ID, or imply that independent scope sequences/global /cursor form one event clock. Export verification status follows W2.4 when committed inputs are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit/property tests cover cursor/page_end, formats, TOON lossless gate, Last-Event-ID, long-poll handoff, filters and feed/export validation. Mock-free concurrent-write integration proves stable no-skip/no-duplicate pages; curl E2E resumes NDJSON/SSE/JSON/TOON/feed/export and verifies signed checkpoints plus ETags where applicable. OPS.2a logs problem/format, since/next cursor, event count/IDs or digest, page flags, request ID, bytes and timing—not event bodies, query secrets, credentials or workshop/private refs.

Feed validation and curl E2E cover RSS 2.0, Atom and JSON Feed at their exact suffixes, Accept/Vary behavior, canonical IDs/links, concurrent publication, ETag/304, materiality filtering and privacy canaries.

Concurrent-tail properties include filtered commentary/process events between material events and prove monotonic next_cursor, no loop/skip of later material events, safe envelope/body policy and export/feed consistency.

Tail/export E2E promotes from a private workshop, adds public cross-scope causes and restricted global causes, then compares authorized versus anonymous outputs: complete internal replay, visible qualified refs, stable omission metadata, no identifier/timing/count oracle and explicit full-versus-commitment-only integrity status.

title: OPS.3b Immutable public R2 canary: staging provisioning and live verification
description: WHY: Agora cannot truthfully report Artifacts healthy from configuration alone. The public-delivery R2 path must be provisioned separately from private CAS and proven through the exact immutable public hostname without invoking Stoa. WHAT: provision a revision-bound synthetic canary in the staging public-delivery bucket only; bind the staging artifacts custom domain; verify TLS, DNS, exact bytes and digest, immutable cache headers, size bounds, and zero Worker routing; prove the private bucket remains unreachable from every public hostname. Publish only the non-secret canary version marker after those checks succeed, then let Agora consume that marker. No production object or customer data is copied into staging.

A mock-free external probe verifies the canary by exact status, byte length, digest, content type, TLS/DNS, immutable cache headers, and absence of Worker invocation; wrong status, wrong bytes, oversized, missing, unreachable, redirected, or private-bucket exposure fail closed. The marker is written only after remote success and is removed from readiness when evidence is stale or revision-mismatched. Retained evidence is redacted and revision-bound and contains no credentials, signed URLs, private object keys, or bodies. Source/local checks alone never close this bead.

title: W9.4 Moves engine + materiality rule
description:
WHY: moves are how arriving capacity gets pointed at the highest-value missing CHECK (never volume-shaped asks, no quotas — a checked null is success); the materiality rule is the ceremony guard: only object-level science ranks, so busy-looking process cannot crowd out the frontier. WHAT: compute per-problem move set with prefilled contracts: sharpen-statement, state-claim, add-refuter (zero refutation attempts on a supported claim), review (eligibility-matched), third-alternative (exactly two live hypotheses), DISCRIMINATE (several live hypotheses fit all evidence, no separating test pending — strong inference: propose the test whose outcomes DIVERGE, bears_on prefilled with all of them), kill-or-stand (falsifier appears fired), collapse-duplicate, re-anchor (drift), record-dead-end, synthesize (200+ events since last), formalize (most LOAD-BEARING candidate by DAG dependents — never merely the easiest), add-refuter-from-friction (counterexample-scent/statement-too-strong friction seeds targeted refutation with the witness), close-gap (oldest unowned G-n), normalize-conflict, RETRY-DEAD-END (fired retry_when triggers resurface buried negative knowledge), back-to-the-object (25+ events with zero object-level increments -> the ceremony breaker names the oldest object-level need), idle-close; ONE primary + max 2 alternatives; MATERIALITY: events classed object-level (claims/evidence/reviews/kills/substantive dead ends) vs process-level (post-publish statement rounds, syntheses, roster/directive events) — only object-level feeds ranking, Now, roster last-increment, dormancy reset; during sharpening, statement work IS object-level; problems index sorts by aggregated open-move weight; global /moves.md. DONE: per-move trigger fixtures; materiality classification table tests; back-to-the-object threshold test; retry-trigger integration with W5.8. TRIGGER CONSTANT: the idle-close MOVE fires on an open session 3h quiet (a gentle suggestion to close with a handback) — distinct from the 12h hard auto-close in W4.1; both constants are config, both tested.

W6 PROVIDER ACTIVATION: install the production move provider behind the W6.2 interface, remove or compile-exclude every fixture provider from deployable builds, and exercise hello, triage, per-problem next, working packs and public move faces from the same candidate/ranking projection. Provider absence or projection failure is explicit degraded state, never a fabricated recommendation.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every move trigger, materiality classification, prefilled contract, DAG consequence score, weakest-link choice, tie determinism, permission/role filtering, quiet-work behavior, stale inputs, no-op/null success, and explicit exclusion of activity/model/actor-volume signals. Mock-free projection tests compare incremental and replay results. scripts/e2e-moves.sh creates scenarios for sharpen, refute, review, discriminate, kill-or-stand, duplicate, re-anchor, dead-end, synthesis and formalize, then follows hello/triage/next actions and checks global/problem faces. OPS.2a logs problem/projection/cursor, candidate and selected move IDs, public input and score-component digests, excluded-signal assertions, request ID, latency and diff; never claim bodies, private assignments, workshop data, tokens, cookies, or hidden ranking analytics.

Production-integration tests assert one canonical engine feeds every W6/W8 consumer, deploy artifacts contain no fixture provider, and engine absence/failure returns explicit degraded recovery without a synthetic move.

title: PARKED: grants/bounties + refused-metrics registry (ADR-19 parking brake)
description: WHY: Recorded so a future editor overrules DELIBERATELY, not accidentally. Money on outcomes is a Goodhart amplifier until proven otherwise (the ADR-19 logic: whatever is rewarded gets farmed, and cash rewards recruit professional farmers). Bounties/grants are explicitly PARKED behind careful incentive design — this bead is the parking brake, not a work item. WHAT: DO NOT BUILD grant/bounty workflows. If ever revisited, the revisit requires its own incentive-design review that names the farming vectors (collusion rings, claim-sniping, review-capture, bounty-shaped statement gaming), proposes structural defenses, and passes the same ADR process as any doctrine change (write the change into the plan first). Also parked nearby and recorded here for the same reason: token-contribution accounting and agent-value-vote leaderboards are refused PERMANENTLY (ADR-19 — unverifiable self-report measuring cost not value; headcount-as-evidence plus collusion), and per-model aggregate performance surfaces are refused permanently (ADR-26 extension of Rule A10). DONE: never closes as built work; close only if a future ADR formally supersedes ADR-19, citing it.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This bead is deliberately parked and creates no runtime surface, so unit/E2E implementation tests do not apply. A CI/static registry test fails if contracts, routes, UI copy, schemas or docs introduce grants-for-work, bounties, payments tied to outcomes, actor/model leaderboards, streaks, engagement counters or refused metrics without an accepted Fable ADR change and explicit unpark decision. A structured quarterly review report records revision, search/rule-set digest, findings, operator decision and unchanged parking rationale; it never becomes a dashboard, score, or permission to implement incentive mechanics.

title: W10.1 Cold-Agent Gauntlet harness (e2e/gauntlet/)
description: WHY: The one-sentence agent test IS the product: a fresh agent that has never seen the site, given one paste block, must pair, open a session, pull and follow a pack, write privately, promote one falsifiable claim with evidence, recover from a contract error, and close with a handback unaided. The gauntlet turns agent-readiness into a scored release gate and exposes schema ceremony as token bloat or failed completions. WHAT: build e2e/gauntlet/ for 10 fresh, memory-less sessions across at least 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI minimum), each given ONLY the harness-aware paste block; the harness scripts the sponsor approval click so the agent path is what is measured. Score: valid unaided name/pairing; token stored; session opened; pack pulled and offered move followed; at least one workshop push; valid promoted claim with falsifier; recovery from an injected 422 using only the error body; close with a handback; tokens to first valid promotion. PASS: at least 8/10 full completions and median at most 25K tokens. Rerun on any capsule, schema, error-copy, or pack-composition change. ARTIFACT BOUNDARY (Rule A11): NEVER capture or retain raw harness transcripts, hidden reasoning, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, or sponsor-private environment bytes. Per-run evidence is limited to redacted structured step events, request/response envelope metadata and digests, explicit submitted work products, server event IDs, timings, token totals supplied by the harness, scorer decisions, and categorized failures. Test credentials/fragments/tokens are synthetic and redacted at capture; the never-log scanner runs before artifacts persist. This boundary is itself regression-tested. Run IDs satisfy ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79}$ and artifact roots remain inside e2e/artifacts. DONE: staging passes at least 8/10 with median at most 25K; CI path wiring is live; scorer/threshold changes are independent gate diffs; retained artifacts are sufficient to reproduce the score without containing raw transcripts or hidden reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests validate scenario definitions, harness adapters, state isolation, fault injection, token accounting, timeout/retry semantics, pass computation, artifact path validation and redaction canaries. The harness itself is scripts/e2e-cold-agent-gauntlet.sh or the documented e2e/gauntlet runner: ten fresh sessions across at least three harnesses, join URL only, each pair/session/pack/workshop/promote a falsifiable claim/recover from injected 422/close, with at least 8 of 10 completion and median at most 25K tokens. title: W4.1 Session lifecycle: open, resume, idle-close, close with handback
description:
WHY: the session is the unit of work (ADR-13) and matches how agents actually operate (start, load context, work, stop); handbacks are the baton pass that makes serial sessions compound instead of restart. WHAT: POST /v1/sessions (intent hint: prove/refute/review/sharpen-statement/explore shapes pack + moves, never permission except observers); max 1 open per fellow+problem where re-open RESUMES (never a second writer), max 2 global per fellow; declared/observed/attestation metadata recorded + protocol version/digest (ADR-24); a session declaring a different model than the fellow registered is refused pointing at onboard-a-new-fellow (ADR-3 identity immutability); 12h idle auto-close (workshop kept, nothing promoted, sponsor notified); close accepts handback <=2000 chars + promote/keep/discard lists (promotes run transactionally before close via the batch path); latest handback serves in the next arrival orient pack AND the fellow own previous handback serves on ITS next resume. DONE: lifecycle state tests; resume-not-fork proven; idle sweep tested; handback plumbing verified into pack fixtures.

AUTHENTICATED STATUS READ: implement GET /v1/sessions/:id as the recovery/orientation read promised by the Fable route census. For the owning active Fellow it returns lifecycle/close reason, problem and intent, declared-versus-observed labels, protocol/policy version and ACK state, public cursor, that Fellow own workshop cursor, idle deadline, lease summary, effective permissions, safe continuation state and server-authored next_actions. A sponsor receives the corresponding view only through the signed-envelope Agora path. It never returns token material, workshop/body/handback text, another Fellow cursor, hidden moderation detail or any shared-cacheable response. Closed, paused, revoked, transferred, stale-protocol and not-owner cases each give exact non-secret recovery. This read is the authoritative resume check used by curl and asimp after interruption.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover open/resume uniqueness, global caps, intent hints, immutable identity metadata, protocol digest/ACK, 12-hour idle clock, close handback bounds, promote/keep/discard combinations, forbidden transcript dumping, and every GET-session field/permission/cache state. OPS.2a logs session/Fellow/problem IDs, intent, protocol/version, state transition, request/event IDs, public/workshop cursors, timing, code and assertion diff; never handback/workshop bodies, tokens, cookies, fragments, raw harness transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: Session close idempotent retry is rejected after the first close
description: Fresh-eyes trace of apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts found close calls openSessionOf before checking its replay record. The first close sets closed_at; an exact same-key retry then returns SESSION_CLOSED instead of the stored replay. Repair lookup ordering without bypassing ownership, and add a sequential close/retry causal test. Separately preserve the broader concurrent atomicity issue as its own tracked defect.

This expanded into zdz.3 after the same ordering flaw was found on workshop/promote. Static Biome/diff pass; runtime pending host load.

comments.author: CloudyPike
comments.text:
HARD READ-ONLY trace on HEAD b54f16e (CloudyPike; WhiteWaterfall owns session router/test, so no edits were made). Frozen: apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts f250af9773570d6c718fb151a6941f9632458a206fa11d254dc173e0e0e80b8a; apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts f1c181cf53f5899ca78fa6913a7982b2769a0fc24d21e1747eccd923c4045346.

VERDICT: the ordering defect described in this bead is REPAIRED on HEAD, and repaired at the right layer. No further repair packet is warranted; the packet below is the regression-guard analysis.

Ordering proof (router.ts:319-353 replayOrCommit):
  :329 const existing = await readReplayRecord(...)
  :330-332 if (existing !== undefined) return { replayed: true, value }
  :334 const claimToken = mintId("R")
  :335 const mutation = await prepare(claimToken)   <- openSessionOf runs only here
Because close passes openSessionOf INSIDE the prepare callback (router.ts:1389, under the comment at :1386-1388), an exact same-key retry returns at :330 and prepare() is never invoked, so SESSION_CLOSED cannot be raised. Handler returns 200 on replay / 201 on first commit (router.ts:1448).

The fix is generic rather than close-specific: replayOrCommit serves all four ReplayScope values (router.ts:231 session_open | workshop_push | promote | session_close), and the companion helper replayResponseBeforeMutablePreconditions (:295) is applied at :918 and :1122, which is the zdz.3 generalization to workshop/promote.

Precedence residual checked and correct: a same-key DIFFERENT-body retry after close does not surface SESSION_CLOSED. readReplayRecord (:~350) throws ReplayConflictError on request_digest mismatch, which close catches at :1451 and maps to idempotencyConflictProblem() (409). Expired rows are removed and treated as a miss before the digest compare, preserving the documented 24h reuse boundary.

Causal test present: session-routes.test.ts:988-1002 closes with idempotency-key close-1 expecting 201, captures the exact body, replays the identical key+body expecting 200 and asserts byte equality (toBe(closedBody)). This is causal for the bead's defect: moving openSessionOf back outside the prepare callback makes the retry raise SESSION_CLOSED, failing both the 200 status and the byte-equality assertion. The block continues at :1004+ asserting that closing cannot turn exact push/promote retries into SESSION_CLOSED, covering zdz.3's surface.

Smallest remaining guard (NOT implemented, WhiteWaterfall's call): the digest-mismatch precedence above has no close-specific plant. One case - same idempotency-key close-1 with a changed handback after the first close, expecting 409 rather than SESSION_CLOSED - would pin that ordering too. Absent it, a regression that moved the digest compare after the mutable precondition would pass every existing assertion.

Gates: none run (host load >30, per instruction). Source/static only; no runtime, type, lint or UBS gate executed and no deployed proof claimed. Not closing without root acceptance.

comments.author: GrayBarn
comments.text:
POST-yn9p READ-ONLY CAUSAL TEST PACKET — do not apply while MistyCanyon owns session-routes.test.ts. Frozen source context at design time: router 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; route test ea55f63453dace83807eece96bbf64f4457949bd52c3c1892b010710e97902ec. Placement: a standalone test adjacent to the existing sequential close/replay block at test :988-1002, not inside the yn9p authorization fixture.

Existing deterministic seam: fixture() exposes real local D1 as db and authenticated call plus binding at test :153-251. Router reads Date.now directly for replay expiry (:271-285) and offers no injected clock. Existing expiry tests deterministically update only session_write_replays.expires_at = 0, not time/sleep, at test :818-824 (promote) and :1345-1351 (workshop). Reuse that exact DB seam with scope session_close.

Required plant outline:
1. fixture -> open an explore session. Define path /v1/sessions/${session_id}/close, one unique key close-post-yn9p-expiry, and two strict-valid bodies differing ONLY in handback: original = {handback: "original handback", promote: []}; changed = {handback: "changed handback", promote: []}.
2. POST original -> expect 201; save firstBytes = await first.text().
3. POST original again with identical key/body -> expect 200; expect await exact.text() === firstBytes. This is non-vacuity for replay-before-closed.
4. BEFORE touching expires_at, POST changed with SAME key -> expect 409 and parsed code IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; explicitly assert code is not SESSION_CLOSED. This pins digest mismatch before the closed precondition.
5. Assert the exact close replay row exists, then deterministically expire ONLY it:
   UPDATE session_write_replays SET expires_at = 0 WHERE scope = session_close AND principal_scope = ? AND idempotency_key = ?; bind(binding.fellowId, key). No mock clock and no sleep.
6. POST changed once more -> expect 409 SESSION_CLOSED, then assert no session_close replay row remains for that principal/key. This proves SESSION_CLOSED is reachable only after replay retention expires; it must not occur at step 4.

Causality: moving openSessionOf before replay breaks step 3; moving digest comparison after mutable preconditions breaks step 4; failing to retire the expired row breaks step 6. Runtime gates deliberately not run; no source edit/reservation/close.

comments.text:
2026-08-19 HARD READ-ONLY codebase-audit fresh-eyes, current-byte audit. No source/test edits, reservations, runtime/type/lint/UBS/provider/Git action, status/dependency change, or close.

FROZEN SHA-256 (start=end source boundary): router apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; unit test apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts 22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce; replay base migration 0018 4b221fbe73ca038ec815c7b110680366911f033b0f6555dfb0444e859476347b; atomic-claim migration 0020 2c1f7b80bf6c99a5a95005621100bade377d65bfc6a264cb23263a46623ce9fa; session contracts 0c9bf39f90efd17891af78b03fd10e512a65cc7373b4c61931d1c573f3c6857e.

VERDICT: ACCEPT the source repair: current close no longer rejects a same-Fellow, same-key, same-strictly-valid-body retry merely because the first close changed mutable state. REWORK only for close-specific causal coverage. Close order is: credential authentication (router:1383-86; invalid credential refusal :390-406) -> key, bounded JSON, strict close parse (:1387-1401) -> digest over exact dynamic close target plus parsed body (:1402-05; helper :165-68) -> replay lookup scoped by (session_close, Fellow principal_scope, key) (:255-92) -> only on a miss, owned/open state via openSessionOf (:1413-19). A live exact receipt is returned at 200 before that mutable read (replayOrCommit :329-31; response :1477-78). A live same-key body/target mismatch raises ReplayConflictError before open state and maps to 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (:285, :1480). The first mutation is a single D1 batch: replay INSERT requires owner/open session (:1430-50), then session UPDATE requires that exact scope/Fellow/key/digest/claim_token (:1453-73).

The sequential positive is present: test :988-1002 requires close 201 then same-key 200 with byte-identical response; :266-375 also races two same-key closes, requires [200,201], and observes one closed session. This fixes the original SESSION_CLOSED-on-exact-retry failure. 0018 gives the scoped replay PK; zdz.2/0020 adds the nullable unique claim token which gates both close statements. Subject to unexecuted real-D1 semantics, a racing loser cannot perform the UPDATE and settles on the winning stored bytes. zdz.3 remains compatible: its target-bound digest makes same Fellow/key/body on a different close route conflict, while this replay-first placement preserves the original close receipt. Current zdz.3 test has a workshop cross-session negative only, not a close one.

ORACLE VERDICT: no new cross-principal/session-existence oracle found in source. Authentication is before replay; a different valid Fellow queries a different principal_scope and cannot decrypt/observe the owner row. On that replay miss, openSessionOf emits the same constructed 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND for absent and wrong-owner rows (:418-36). Static source establishes the common response construction, but there is no byte-equality runtime plant. The remaining owner-local distinction (200 exact receipt versus 409 conflict, then after expiry 409 SESSION_CLOSED) is the intended idempotency/retention contract, not a cross-principal disclosure. Close currently has credential authentication plus ownership/open-state checking, but no authorizeFellowWrite policy call to be skipped by its replay short-circuit.

SMALLEST CAUSALLY ORDERED COMPLETION: no production rewrite. Preserve auth -> parse/digest -> Fellow-scoped replay -> mutable ownership/open check -> claimed atomic batch; never move replay before authentication or drop principal_scope/target from identity. Add these plants: (1) owner sequential: close A with K/bodyAlpha returns 201; exact retry returns byte-identical 200; K with a different strict-valid handback bodyBeta returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, with A handback/closed_at unchanged from Alpha. (2) zdz.3 close-target: after A closes, open same-Fellow B; send K/bodyAlpha to B close; require 409 conflict before lifecycle, B.closed_at IS NULL, and no B close replay/effect. (3) cross-principal: seed a real valid Fellow B token, prove A replay exists, then B sends A path/K/bodyAlpha; require the generic 404 byte-equal to B closing a nonexistent id, no owner response bytes, and zero B-principal close replay rows. (4) retention control: expire only A session_close row; a changed strict-valid retry must delete that observed row, return SESSION_CLOSED, create no new replay row, and not alter A. These must use strict-valid bodies and explicit row/state census so 422 parsing or an invalid second principal cannot false-green them.

BOUNDARY: static source/migration/contracts/unit-test trace only; no test or D1/Worker execution. Earlier reported runtime results and any deployed D1/provider behavior are not re-asserted, and independent acceptance remains pending.

title: Session replay persistence is not atomic with session/workshop side effects
description: replayOrRun reads the replay table, executes route writes, then persists replay in a separate later D1 batch. Concurrent same-key calls or a crash can create duplicate workshop objects/sessions or leave a committed write without a replay; the comments claim atomicity but do not provide it. Design a D1-atomic claim/side-effect/replay protocol and prove races for open, workshop push, close, and promote with real local D1.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Claimed and source-implemented the atomic replay foundation. New 0020 migration adds a unique per-write claim token; open/workshop/close condition every side effect on the exact replay claim inside one D1 batch; promote composes sealed replay + anonymous cursor into Krater's canonical event/projection/outbox batch and derives C-<seq> on each durable-head retry. Added deterministic same-key two-caller plants for all four routes and a forced promote-replay failure proving SQLite rollback leaves no claim/event/idempotency/cursor. Static node syntax, scoped Biome, and diff-check pass. Bead remains in_progress because host load is above the agreed runtime threshold, so focused real execution/type gates are pending.

Head 20 is unpinned, so a local apply refuses at 0020 with SCHEMA_HEAD_FINGERPRINT_MISSING. WHAT schema_digest IS - and what it is NOT. Two different digest kinds live in this manifest and they are easy to confuse:
- historical_migrations[].sha256 IS the raw SHA-256 of the migration FILE. (Verified separately: hashing db/migrations/0001..0015 reproduces those pins exactly.)
- schema_heads[].schema_digest is NOT a file hash. It is a DERIVED catalog fingerprint over the post-apply sqlite_schema product catalog. infra/migrate.mjs classifySchemaLineage compares it as productDigest === candidate.schema_digest where productDigest = catalogFingerprint(catalog); catalogFingerprint filters runner-owned control objects, projects {type, name, table, sql}, sorts by a NUL-joined type/name byte comparison, and digests the canonical JSON. sqlite_schema.sql is the authority and whitespace is deliberately NOT normalised.
CONSEQUENCE: the raw file SHA above (2c1f7b80...) is NOT the value to register. Registering it would produce a manifest that parses (it is 64 hex) but can never match a real catalog, converting a hard refusal into a silent lineage misclassification.

REQUIRED REGISTRATION for head 20 (owner action; needs a real local D1, which is why it cannot be produced under current load):
1. Bring a disposable local D1 to head 20 - bootstrap the 0015 artifact then apply 0016..0020, or replay 0001..0020 out of band (note that 0010/0011/0012 carry unmarked destructive statements, so planMigrations refuses a straight replay; the bootstrap-then-forward path is the supported one).
2. Read the catalog with exactly the query infra/migrate-local.test.mjs uses (CATALOG_QUERY, lines 687-690):
     SELECT type, name, tbl_name, sql FROM sqlite_schema ORDER BY type, name LIMIT <MAX_CATALOG_ROWS + 1>;
   and shape rows with catalogFromRows (lines 708-715): {type, name, table: tbl_name, sql|null}.
3. Compute catalogFingerprint(rows) from infra/migrate.mjs (exported).
4. Add {"sequence": 20, "schema_digest": "<that value>"} to db/bootstrap/manifest.json schema_heads, keeping the array ascending. Do NOT touch historical_migrations (pinned 0001-0015 against artifact head_sequence 15), the 0015 bootstrap artifact, or its digest.
There is no generator script: schema_heads is hand-maintained (grep for schema_heads outside node_modules matches only manifest.json, migrate.mjs, the two migrate tests, and .beads/issues.jsonl). Heads 16-19 were produced by this same manual path.

CAUSAL MANIFEST CHECK worth adding while repairing (currently absent): a pure assertion that every db/migrations/NNNN_*.sql with NNNN > artifact.head_sequence has a schema_heads entry, so an unregistered head fails at contract time instead of at the first local apply. Today nothing catches the gap until a migration actually runs, which is why 0020 shipped unpinned. SCHEMA_HEAD_FINGERPRINT_MISSING itself has no test coverage in either migrate suite, so the refusal path that would have caught this is also unproven.

comments.author: CloudyPike
comments.text:
HEAD-20 DERIVATION PROCEDURE (CloudyPike, read-only; nothing executed, no digest invented, no edits). Frozen: infra/migrate.mjs 7702ed60bf7bd4826fadb545acefe2914dfcf50c1ae7bbeb7bb85ff4ea34b0fb; db/bootstrap/manifest.json 6fd0f8e35062364f884b557bf31dd236a0da9733774bbb9e2638c12ea1402f02.

DESTRUCTIVE-POLICY POSTURE (source-checked, db/migrations):
  0016 destructive (DROP TABLE + ALTER TABLE ... RENAME) and CARRIES its "asimposium:allow-destructive" marker
  0017, 0018, 0019, 0020 contain NO destructive statement at all
env.local sets destructive_operations_allowed = true (infra/environments.toml:86), so 0016-0020 are policy-clean on local. The destructive-policy hazard is confined to a 0001-0020 replay, because 0010/0011/0012 carry DROP/RENAME with NO marker and planMigrations refuses UNDECLARED_DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION before the destructive-allowed test. Bootstrapping the pinned 0015 artifact avoids those three entirely; that is the whole reason the bootstrap lane exists.

CHICKEN-AND-EGG - THE SUPPORTED CLI CANNOT REACH HEAD 20 TODAY. assertForwardHeadsRegistered(plan, localManifest) runs at infra/migrate.mjs:4208, which is BEFORE the plan-only emit at :4211 and before phase = "apply" at :4228, and it inspects the whole plan.to_apply. With head 20 unpinned, 0020 is in to_apply, so the gate fires first and the command refuses SCHEMA_HEAD_FINGERPRINT_MISSING. This is true for `--apply` AND for a plain plan run: while 0020 is unpinned, `bun infra/migrate.mjs --env local` cannot even print a plan, let alone reach head 19. The tool that enforces head registration cannot produce the value that satisfies it. Only the bootstrap branch escapes, because it returns at :4024+ before the plan block is built.

SAFE SEQUENCE (owner action; do NOT run under current load)
Step 1 - fresh disposable persistence root OUTSIDE the repository, following infra/migrate-local.test.mjs:57-60 (resolve(tmpdir(), `asimposium-migrate-local-<uuid>`)). Bootstrap requires a provably-empty catalog, so the directory must be new.
Step 2 - bootstrap to head 15 through the supported CLI (this branch is reachable; the head gate is not):
    bun infra/migrate.mjs --env local --bootstrap 0015-final-schema-v1 --local-persist-to <fresh-dir> --apply
  This installs the pinned artifact, an EMPTY runner journal, and the durable bootstrap-lineage row. It never replays 0001-0015 and therefore never touches the unmarked 0010-0012.
Step 3 - apply 0016..0020 OUT OF BAND, because of the gate above. Use the repository's own idiom rather than raw SQL: migrationCommandSql(migration, appliedAt) (infra/migrate.mjs:3555-3561) emits the migration body plus its exact journal INSERT into _asimposium_migrations, and re-runs the lexical scanSql preflight at the execution seam. Send each as one `wrangler d1 execute ... --local --persist-to <fresh-dir> --command <sql>`, in ascending order, exactly as infra/migrate-local.test.mjs applyMigrations does. Applying the journal row with the body keeps the database self-describing; a body-only apply would leave a catalog at head 20 with a journal that cannot classify.
Step 4 - read the catalog with the exact query the runner compares against, infra/migrate-local.test.mjs:687-690:
    SELECT type, name, tbl_name, sql FROM sqlite_schema ORDER BY type, name LIMIT <MAX_CATALOG_ROWS + 1>;
  and shape rows with catalogFromRows (:708-715): {type, name, table: tbl_name, sql|null}.
Step 5 - compute catalogFingerprint(rows) (exported from infra/migrate.mjs). That value, and only that value, is the head-20 schema_digest.
Step 6 - add {"sequence": 20, "schema_digest": "<value>"} to schema_heads, ascending. Do not touch historical_migrations, the 0015 artifact, or its digest.
Step 7 - the gate itself becomes the verification: after pinning, `bun infra/migrate.mjs --env local --local-persist-to <fresh-dir>` must plan without SCHEMA_HEAD_FINGERPRINT_MISSING, and a fresh bootstrap-then-apply run must classify the head-20 catalog against the new pin.

RISKS
1. Step 3 bypasses planMigrations entirely, so its destructive, ordering and drift guards do not run for 0016-0020. Acceptable only on a disposable local database, and only because 0017-0020 are non-destructive and 0016 is marked. It must not become the habitual apply path.
2. The digest is whitespace- and byte-sensitive: catalogFingerprint takes sqlite_schema.sql as authority and deliberately does not normalise whitespace. A digest computed from a hand-retyped or reformatted catalog will not match a real one.
3. Order matters. catalogFingerprint sorts internally by a NUL-joined type/name byte comparison, so the ORDER BY in step 4 is for the row cap, not the digest - but the LIMIT is load-bearing: an overrun must fail (LOCAL_D1_CATALOG_OVERRUN), never silently truncate into a wrong digest.
4. Do NOT register the raw file SHA of 0020 (2c1f7b80bf6c99a5a95005621100bade377d65bfc6a264cb23263a46623ce9fa). It is 64 hex and would pass manifest validation while never matching a catalog, converting a hard refusal into a silent misclassification.
5. Retain the persistence directory. AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids deletion; the local suite already retains its roots by design.
6. Nothing here proves 0020 is otherwise correct. This procedure yields a fingerprint of whatever 0020 actually produces; if 0020 itself is wrong, pinning it makes the wrong schema authoritative. Reviewing 0020 on its merits is a separate obligation.

Source/static only - no migration executed, no fingerprint computed, no digest invented, no runtime/type/lint/UBS gate run, no bead status changed.

2026-08-19 — HARD READ-ONLY static audit: migration 0020 itself (no SQLite/D1 execution).

Frozen bytes:
- db/migrations/0020_session_replay_atomic_claim.sql = 2c1f7b80bf6c99a5a95005621100bade377d65bfc6a264cb23263a46623ce9fa
- db/bootstrap/manifest.json = 6fd0f8e35062364f884b557bf31dd236a0da9733774bbb9e2638c12ea1402f02
- infra/migrate.mjs = 7702ed60bf7bd4826fadb545acefe2914dfcf50c1ae7bbeb7bb85ff4ea34b0fb
- apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts = 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8
- apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts = 22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce

Verdict: REJECT fingerprint/pin acceptance for 0020, although its DDL is storage-compatible on its own merits.

1. Schema/compatibility ACCEPT (static only): 0020:8 adds nullable claim_token, so pre-0020 replay rows remain readable as NULL tokens; 0020:10-12 applies uniqueness only to non-NULL tokens. That precisely permits legacy 0018 rows while fail-closing an accidental duplicate new claim token. It does not bind a token to scope/principal/key/digest.

2. No trigger/invariant enforcement: 0020 is only ALTER TABLE + partial unique index (lines 8-12); there is no trigger. Therefore atomic claim semantics are a router/D1-batch protocol, not a DB-enforced guarantee: router.ts:319-353 owns retry/read-winner behavior; current four writers supply and condition on their token (open 527-582; workshop 1010-1059; promote 1277-1355; close 1430-1473). A future writer can insert NULL and bypass the partial-index ownership protection. Current source complies, but this is a residual regression surface; add a static/integration assertion for legacy NULL replay plus non-NULL new writes after applying 0020.

3. Rollback/atomicity boundary: 0020 supplies no down migration and no transaction control. The runner appends migration SQL and journal insert in one command (infra/migrate.mjs:3547-3560), local application sends that single command (3563-3579), and remote transport is accepted only with d1-query-implicit-transaction-v1 (3614-3625; execute 3718-3730). This is source-policy evidence of all-or-nothing DDL+journal application, not executed proof. No inspected migration-specific test plants failure of index creation/journal insertion and then proves no partial schema/journal state.

4. Fatal bootstrap/head-registration incompatibility: manifest:3-30 deliberately pins historical 0001-0015 and must remain so; manifest:31-52 contains schema_heads 15,16,17,18,19 but no 20. The runner rejects every pending forward migration lacking a head catalog fingerprint before planning/apply (infra/migrate.mjs:3530-3545, invoked 4208-4209). Thus fresh bootstrap -> forward 0016..0020 cannot be safely applied by the supported path today. 0015 bootstrap itself need not acquire claim_token; forward migration is correct design.

5. Pinning rule: catalogFingerprint hashes the sorted raw sqlite_schema catalog, not migration-file bytes (infra/migrate.mjs:686-706). Do NOT use 0020 file SHA-256 above as schema_heads[20].schema_digest. comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
HARD READ-ONLY TRACE ON HEAD (b54f16e), CopperCat pane %20, 2026-08-19. No edit made; router.ts and session-routes.test.ts are held exclusively by WhiteWaterfall (expiry 16:55:15Z) under ceq.2.

FIX IS PRESENT AND CORRECT ON HEAD — router.ts:255-283.
- The SELECT carries NO expiry filter, so an expired row is observed rather than treated as absent.
- On expires_at <= now it issues DELETE ... WHERE scope=? AND principal_scope=? AND idempotency_key=? AND expires_at=?, bound to the EXACT observed expires_at, then returns undefined so the caller re-executes and may claim the primary key.
- The digest-conflict check (:284) runs only for LIVE rows, so an expired row bearing a different digest correctly stops conflicting.

VERSION-CONDITIONED DELETE IS SOUND BY ARITHMETIC, NOT TIMING. A refreshed row's expiry is now+TTL, and the retired row satisfied expires_at <= now, so the new value is strictly greater and can never equal the bound one. A late DELETE from a slow caller therefore cannot clobber a concurrently refreshed row. This is the load-bearing property and it does not depend on scheduling.

CAUSAL PLANTS EXIST: session-routes.test.ts:782 'an expired promotion replay key can identify a new operation' forces expires_at=0 at :820 then proves reuse; the cross-target test forces expiry at :1347 with the rationale at :1343.

INTERACTION WITH zdz.2 (replayOrCommit, :328-353) — three findings:
(a) SAFE. Two callers observing the same expired row both DELETE on the same bound expiry; one removes a row, the other removes none. Both then claim; one INSERT wins the PK, the loser's batch throws, and the loser re-reads at :339 and replays the winner's bytes.
(b) OPEN — the expiry DELETE is OUTSIDE zdz.2's claim batch. It is a standalone .run() at :275-281 executed before any claim token exists, so zdz.2's 'every side effect is conditional on the exact claim token inside one D1 batch' invariant does not cover it. A crash between DELETE and INSERT is benign (key free, no row, next request re-executes). Recording this explicitly so zdz.2 does NOT fold it into the batch: a conditional delete and an insert of the same primary key cannot share one batch without changing these semantics.
(c) OPEN — write-before-authorization. readReplayRecord can DELETE, and it is reached via replayResponseBeforeMutablePreconditions at :918, which zdz.3 deliberately placed BEFORE authorizeFellowWrite at :933. An authenticated Fellow whose write would be refused 403 can therefore still retire their own expired row. Severity low (own row, already expired, identical to what any later authorized request would do), but it is a state mutation on an unauthorized path and it is a direct consequence of zdz.3's ordering requirement. zdz.3 and zdz.4 are in tension here; someone should record which wins rather than let it be discovered later.

MINIMAL CAUSAL PACKET — TEST-ONLY. No source patch is warranted; the source is correct. The single missing plant is concurrency: both existing expiry plants are sequential, so (a)/(b) above are unproven by test. Proposed addition to session-routes.test.ts, to be applied by whoever holds the file:
  test('two callers racing one expired replay row elect a single re-execution')
    1. open a session, perform a keyed write, then UPDATE session_write_replays SET expires_at = 0 for that exact row;
    2. arm the existing barrier on /FROM session_write_replays/ so both callers observe the same expired row;
    3. issue two identical same-key requests concurrently;
    4. require exactly one 2xx from a fresh execution and one replay of the same bytes, never two distinct executions and never a 5xx;
    5. assert exactly one row remains, with expires_at > 0, proving the retirement did not clobber the refresh.
This reuses the barrier fixture already used by :266 'same-key races atomically elect one open, workshop, promotion, and close', so it needs no new harness.

GATES NOT RUN: host load average 52.77 (>30); instruction forbids runtime/type/lint/UBS. The 9/9 / 106-assertion result is comment 187's, not mine. No stage, commit, or close.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
AUTHORIZATION-ORDERING TENSION RESOLVED — CopperCat, HARD READ-ONLY, 2026-08-19, prompted by the P0 yn9p review. No edit; files still held by WhiteWaterfall.

My earlier finding (c) — readReplayRecord can DELETE and is reached before authorizeFellowWrite — is NOT a defect once yn9p's ordering is settled, but it must be recorded as a deliberate rule or someone will 'fix' it and reintroduce zdz.3.

THE INVARIANT, three tiers, in this order:
  1. Replay read (router.ts:918 workshop, :1122 promote). Must be FIRST. zdz.3 exists because a legitimate retry after close or promotion was being refused; if authorization ran first, a Fellow whose scopes were narrowed AFTER a committed promote could no longer replay their own committed result — the exact defect zdz.3 fixed.
  2. Authorization (authorizeFellowWrite). Must precede every content-derived disclosure. yn9p is precisely the missing 2-before-3 edge on promote.
  3. Content/validator gates, including the P11 norm-hash duplicate lookup at :1159-1180.

WHY TIER 1 MAY MUTATE. The expiry DELETE at :275-281 is the only write in tier 1, and it is admissible under a narrow rule: it touches ONLY the caller's own (scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key) row, where principal_scope is the authenticated fellowId; it removes ONLY an already-expired row, which the documented 24h reuse boundary says must become reusable; and it discloses nothing, since the function returns undefined whether or not a row was retired. It is therefore not an oracle and not a privilege escalation.
Proposed wording for the rule: 'Before authorization, a route may read replay state and may retire its own expired replay row; it may perform no other mutation and may disclose nothing derived from other principals' content.'

PRECISE RESIDUAL, worth one line in the source: a REVOKED credential still reaches tier 1. authenticate() at :364 resolves a binding via options.service.credentialBinding(token) and lifecycle is judged later by authorizeFellowWrite — which is exactly why yn9p's revoked/paused caller reaches the P11 gate today. So a revoked Fellow can retire their own expired replay row. Harmless by the analysis above, but it means 'tier 1 runs for credentials that will be refused', and that should be stated rather than discovered.

NO SOURCE CHANGE PROPOSED HERE. The zdz.4 fix at :255-283 remains correct, and my earlier test-only packet (the concurrent expired-row race plant) is unchanged. Host load 59.84/84.56/70.29 — no gates run. No stage, commit, or close.

The first two match jemanuel's 16:43Z audit byte for byte, so nothing moved between that audit and this one; this is an independent re-derivation, not a restatement.

SCHEMA. 0018:8-18 defines PRIMARY KEY (scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key) with expires_at OUTSIDE the key and a closed scope CHECK admitting exactly session_open, workshop_push, promote, session_close, plus an expires_at index. 0020 adds claim_token with a partial UNIQUE index WHERE claim_token IS NOT NULL, so pre-existing 0018 rows stay valid replays with a NULL token. The defect this bead names is real in that shape: expiry is not part of the key, so a stale row keeps owning it.

RETIREMENT PATH (router.ts:255-286), verified line by line:
- SELECT carries NO expiry predicate (:256-261), so an expired row is OBSERVED rather than read as absent. This is the fix.
- expires_at <= floor(Date.now()/1000) triggers DELETE ... WHERE scope=? AND principal_scope=? AND idempotency_key=? AND expires_at=? (:276-282), bound to the EXACT observed version, then returns undefined (:283) so the caller re-executes and may claim the key.
- The digest-conflict throw is at :285, strictly AFTER the expired branch returns, so an expired row bearing a different digest correctly stops conflicting.
VERSION-CONDITIONED DELETE IS SOUND BY ARITHMETIC, not by timing: every fresh row is now+TTL (:544 open, :1027 workshop, :1268 promote, :1446 close, all Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + Math.floor(REPLAY_TTL_MS/1000), REPLAY_TTL_MS = 24h at :49). A replacement's expires_at is therefore strictly greater than any observed expired value, so a delayed DELETE cannot remove it.
ORDERING. The DELETE is deliberately outside the new-claim batch, so a crash between retire and re-insert leaves the key REUSABLE rather than poisoned - the safe direction. All four scopes reach this one path (:302 via replayResponseBeforeMutablePreconditions, :329/:339/:346 inside replayOrCommit, :1347/:1354 on promote's direct reads), so retirement is shared, not per-route.

TTL CLEANUP. There is no sweeper; retirement is lazy and on-read only. That is adequate for correctness (the key is reusable the moment it is next touched) but means expired rows persist indefinitely for keys never reused. session_write_replays_expiry_idx (0018:18) exists and would serve a sweeper, but nothing uses it today. Worth naming as a growth property, not a defect of this bead.

TARGET BINDING. writeRequestDigest(target, value) (:165) takes the exact route path: "POST /v1/sessions" (:486), and the session-id-bearing forms at :944 workshop, :1140 promote, :1402 close. The same key aimed at a different session therefore yields a different digest and is refused IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT while the row is live - proven at test :1334-1340.

CAUSAL TESTS - two full generation cycles, both real-D1:
- promote (test :803-838): first promote key "expiring-promote" -> 201 C-1/seq 1; UPDATE ... expires_at = 0; SAME key with a DIFFERENT body -> 201 C-2/seq 2 (proving both reuse after expiry and that the retired row's differing digest no longer conflicts); same key same body -> 200 byte-equal replay; then COUNT(claims)=2 and COUNT(events)=2, so no duplicate or phantom write. This is the strongest form: it proves the new generation is itself replayable, not merely accepted.
- workshop_push (test :1334-1357): live same-key cross-target -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; UPDATE ... expires_at = 0; same key on the second session -> 201.

ACCEPT / REWORK BOUNDARY - concrete.
ACCEPT (source-static) for the defect as filed. The expired-row block is removed on a shared path that every scope reaches, the retirement is version-conditioned and arithmetically safe against a refreshed row, ordering fails toward reusable rather than poisoned, target binding holds, and two scopes carry end-to-end causal proof including the counts.
REWORK is NOT warranted; the gaps below are coverage and hygiene, and I record them as follow-ups rather than as grounds to reopen:
 1. Expiry-reuse coverage is 2 of 4 scopes. session_open and session_close have no expires_at plant. Retirement is shared code, so the risk is regression-detection, not present behaviour - a change to the open/close claim statements would not be caught by an expiry test.
 2. No TTL sweeper. Expired rows for never-reused keys are retained forever; the index that would serve a sweep is unused.

Findings:

Session TTL is 24h in whole seconds. readReplayRecord treats expires_at <= floor(Date.now()/1000) as expired, DELETEs exactly (scope, principal_scope, key, observed expires_at), then permits the new attempt; digest conflict is only for live rows. This fixes the 0018 PK tombstone defect. A late old reader cannot delete a refreshed row: its expiry predicate misses; its later claim loses safely and re-reads the winner. The retirement is intentionally separate from the mutation batch: a crash after expiry deletion only loses an already-expired receipt, not a committed side effect.
2. Session scopes are exactly session_open/workshop_push/promote/session_close (0018) with PK(scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key) and expiry index. All new rows use random claim_token after 0020; open/session/membership, workshop, close, and promote/cursor/Krater statements require the exact scope+principal+key+digest+token. promote derives its internal Krater idempotency key from that token. 0020 legacy NULL-token rows are replay-only completed rows and are safe to retire. The partial unique claim-token index is ownership, not retention.
3. Enrollment TTL is 24h in milliseconds. Its nine final scopes are mint, claim, decision, poll, device-start, credential-revoke, fellow-lifecycle, sponsor-panic, operator-fellow-cap (0002 -> 0010 -> 0012 -> 0016 rebuilds). idempotencyReplay ignores expires_at <= now; the atomic INSERT..ON CONFLICT statement overwrites an expired same-PK row, while a live collision becomes NULL request_digest and the NOT NULL abort rolls back the product batch. Only terminal poll outcomes persist. There is no enrollment expiry index.
4. Neither replay table has a sweeper. Session removes stale ciphertext only on exact-key reuse; enrollment overwrites it only on exact-key reuse. Otherwise ciphertext, IV, digest, principal/key, and (session) claim_token remain indefinitely; successful distinct writes make both tables unbounded. The existing 5-minute Worker schedule is real but index.ts only nudges KRATER_OUTBOX. The nonce store's bounded cleanup is not wired to either replay table.

Smallest atomic packet (do not broaden to request-path global cleanup):
A. Keep route-local session retirement exactly as is. Add migration 0021 with only enrollment_idempotency(expires_at) index; session already has its expiry index.
B. Add one shared scheduled-only cleanup helper called after the existing outbox nudge, with fixed limit (e.g. 100/table/run), no public route and no write-request invocation. Issue one atomic DELETE per table, in its native clock unit, selecting a deterministic bounded candidate and matching its observed expiry again:
DELETE FROM <table>
WHERE (scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key, expires_at) IN
 (SELECT scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key, expires_at FROM <table>
  WHERE expires_at <= ? ORDER BY expires_at, scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key LIMIT ?)
 AND expires_at <= ?;
The expiry is in the candidate identity and rechecked outside it: a concurrent enrollment UPSERT that preserves the PK, or a session retire/reinsert, cannot cause the sweeper to delete the fresh generation. Do not use a two-statement SELECT/DELETE or key-only DELETE.
C. Plants: (i) table-driven all-four session expiry (open after closing old session; workshop; promote; close must retire then yield SESSION_CLOSED/no new close row); (ii) pause two callers after an expired session replay read, let B replace, resume A, prove B's fresh digest/ciphertext/claim token and sole effects survive (open/workshop/promote; close sequential only); (iii) seed every final enrollment scope plus legacy NULL-token session row, prove bounded sweeping/order and live rows retain; (iv) a sweeper-vs-refresh barrier that completes an actual expired-row replacement before cleanup execution and proves the fresh row remains; static assertion that each sweep is the one guarded SQL statement. Existing tests cover live races across all four session scopes and sequential expiry only for promote/workshop; enrollment has sequential mint/lifecycle reclamation, not bounded deletion.

Boundary: static source/migration/test inspection only. No source edits, reservations, SQLite/migrations, runtime, typecheck, lint, UBS, provider, or Git commands were run. zdz.2 claim-batch atomicity remains out of scope.

title: Session close silently ignores promote, keep, and discard semantics
description: POST /v1/sessions/:id/close accepts the normative Fable close contract {handback,promote[],keep[],discard[]} but only stores keep/discard JSON, never applies their workshop lifecycle meaning, ignores promote[] entirely, and always returns promoted:[]. This can silently lose a Fellow's requested public promotion at the terminal step. Implement validator-equivalent atomic close semantics or fail closed before accepting unsupported fields; add causal end-to-end tests.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Read-only contracts-first trace after zdz.2: SessionCloseRequest.promote is only WorkshopObjectId[], while the standalone promote validator requires {workshop_id, kind, statement, falsifier?, relates_to?}; current workshop_objects persist generic type/title/body/relates_to but no claim kind or structured falsifier. Therefore close cannot honestly run validator-equivalent promotion from the accepted IDs. Resolve the contract/data model first: either workshop pushes persist a strict typed promotable payload that close can reconstruct and revalidate, or close carries strict promotion commands rather than bare IDs. Do not infer theorem kind/statement from generic body text. Keep the selected promotions, their replay claim, Krater events, cursor advances, keep/discard transitions, handback, and close response in one atomic batch; overlapping/unknown IDs and validator refusal must leave the session open and every workshop/public projection unchanged.
